One more spinning bolt in this body, and down I would go. The previous one had already started the countdown to my body's limit.

Miss the deflection, and there my defeat was settled.

How to do it?

Excellent moving vision, reaction speed, physical ability—not enough. And Kageaki Minato was ordinary in all three. From that side, no possibility at all.

Technique, then. The only chance. Except that the Yoshino style I had learned had no arrow-deflecting technique for this situation.

Bahut achha. Very good. Required subject: not in the syllabus. Time remaining: one breath. Examiner: an arrow, and the bloody examiner would be arriving through my stomach.

So—◆
Now only. Here only. Devise the technique.

One choice, fully reckless.
An outrageous undertaking.
Very little prospect of success.

But unless I caught that spider-thread chance, I would not be permitted to kill that bow knight, that Sagittarius.
ja:
矢が撃ち放たれるまで、おそらくあと一呼吸有るか
無きか。
　その極少時間で無理難題に挑む。

　思い浮かぶ手立ては一つきりだった。

　――矢払いの術。

　飛来する矢を、一剣にて切り落とす。
　入神、極頂の業である。……生身の者にとっては。

　腕に覚えある武者ならば、弓矢はおろか銃弾ですら
太刀一閃にて打ち払うをさしたる難事とはすまい。

　だが武者であっても、同じ武者の弓から放たれる矢
は大いなる脅威と看做みなさねばならなかった。
　弾速において長銃ライフルを凌ぐ武者弓箭の前では、劒冑で
強化された反射神経さえ無意味と堕だすのだ。

　切り払うのは至難の上の最難事。

　……その最難事を俺は成し遂げねばならない。

　それを成さねばこの太刀が敵騎に届かない。
　あの敵を殺せない。

　回転矢ボルトがもう一度、この身体に食い込んだなら、俺
は失墜するだろう。
　先刻の一弾で既に肉体は限界への秒読みカウントダウンを開始して
いるのだ。

　矢を払えなければそこで敗北は決する。

　如何にして、成すか？

　動体視力と反応速度そして運動能力の卓抜をもって、
できる業でないことは明白だ。
　三種のどれ一つとして常人の枠を出ない湊斗景明に
は到底、不可能だ。

　技術をもって挑むのが唯一の可能性だろう。
　しかし俺の学んだ吉野御流は、現況において有効と
なる矢払いの術を伝えていなかった。

　だから――◆
　唯今、即座に、ここで業を工夫する・・・・・・・・・。

　無謀の一択。

　法外の企図だ。
　成功率はごく僅かであろう。

　その蜘蛛の糸のような可能性を掴み取らねば、あの
弓騎士サジタリウスの殺害は許されない。

en:
————Here it came.

My crawling skin, the closing intent to kill, told me less than a second remained.

No leisure to examine methods from every angle. A selection was needed.

In which direction would I think?
Choose that.
ja:
――――来る。

　俺の肌の粟立ちが、敵の殺意の肉迫が、残り時間を
あと一秒弱と告げている。

　多角的視点から方法を検討しているゆとりはない。
〝選択〟が必要だ。

　どの方向で・・・・・考えるか。
　それを選ぼう。

en: Kageaki"————"

Choose first. Think after choosing the direction.

Do not first think about which direction is correct. Just now, that means wasting time. Wasted time means defeat. No other result.

Choose.
ja:
選ぶのだ。考えるのは方向を選んだ後だ。
　正しい方向を知るために考えてはならない。それは
今、時間の浪費しか意味しない。敗北以外の結末を呼
ばない。

〝選択〟をせよ。

en:
Kageaki Minato possessed a vast accumulation of combat experience. Somewhere in it, there should be at least one clue to the right answer.

Choose it.

And one more thing.
Choose the crucial point in the present situation also.

On the basis of that point, examine the combat record and complete an art of combat capable of opposing the enemy's shot.

Then choose.
Select one thing from my past and draw it out.

It was————

Choices
• The battle with Ryoubu Suzukawa.
• The battle with Ukyo Nagasaka.
• The battle with Kotaro Fuma.
• The battle with Ichizo Sorimachi.
• The battle with Konatsu Kurusuno.
• The battle with Shishiku Ootori.
ja:
湊斗景明には膨大な戦闘経験の蓄積がある。
　その中におそらく一つは、正答への手掛かりとなる
ものが含まれている筈だ。

　それを選べ。

　そしてもう一つ。
　現状況下における要点が何であるか、それも選択に
よって決定せよ。

　選んだ要点に基いて戦闘記録を参照、検討し、敵の
射法に対抗し得る戦技アートを完成させることになる。

　では選ぼう。
　俺の過去から一つを選んで引き出そう。

　それは――――

選択肢
• 鈴川令法との戦闘
• 長坂右京との戦闘
• 風魔小太郎との戦闘
• 雪車町一蔵との戦闘
• 来栖野小夏との戦闘
• 大鳥獅子吼との戦闘

en:
And the crucial point was—

Choices
• My injuries.
• The damage to Muramasa.
• The damage to the enemy tsurugi.
• The enemy's eyesight.
• The enemy's objective.
• The worsening weather.
ja:
そして要点は、

選択肢
• 自分の負傷状況
• 村正の損傷状況
• 敵騎の損傷状況
• 敵騎の視力
• 敵騎の目的
• 天候の悪化

en: Hikaru...Hmm. Haan, troublesome situation.HikaruA hint from a past fight, good. But one small condition: you must be able to do the thing. The enemy could do it, very nice for the enemy. Can you? Otherwise what use is the hint?HikaruYou have no concealment technique. Remembering the fellow who concealed himself and made your life difficult—arre, will the memory conceal you? Here that is only wasted effort, no?HikaruNow? Fewer choices already, you see?
ja:
光……むぅ。
　なるほど、厄介な状況だ。光過去の対戦にヒントを求めるのは有効だろ
う。だが問題は、その方法がお前に実行でき・・・・・・・
る・ものでなければ意味がないという点だ。光姿隠しの術を持たないお前が、姿隠しの術
でお前を苦しめた敵のことを参考にしても、
この場合はまるで徒労……そう思わないか。光どうだ？
　選択肢が限られてきただろう？

en: HikaruStruggling, haan.HikaruEven from my side, advice is difficult. Only general principles I can offer... Still, listen to this much.HikaruThe person who holds the strongest weapon often finds it is the thing that kills him.HikaruEverything depended on that weapon. Weapon gone, now the man can do nothing. Or... the enemy turns that strongest weapon's strength against him.HikaruFamiliar story, no? ...Hmm. My own advice. Why is it coming back and slapping me?
ja:
光苦戦しているな。光おれとしても助言が難しい。
　一般論くらいしか言えそうにないが……
　まぁ、一応聞いてゆけ。光最強の武器を持つ者は、往々にして、それ
が命取りとなるものだ。光その武器に頼り切りであったばかりに、失っ
た途端、何もできなくなってしまったり。
　あるいは……最強の武器を敵に逆用・・されて
しまったり、な。光良くある話だろう？
　…………むぅ。
　なんだか自分の言葉が耳に痛いな。

en:
Straight ahead—
I raced with the enemy directly before me.
ja:
真っ直ぐに――
　敵影を正面へ置いて疾駆する。

en:
Sword steady. Point straight ahead.

To meet the enemy's arrow, I also became one arrow. One sharp-pointed instrument for piercing through.

This technique I had learned from Shishiku Ootori. The dazzling sword—put the point exactly where the opponent's vision is focused, upset the balance of mind and senses.

...Yes, I knew. That technique had worked at close quarters.

Warriors in the sky came together from far away at the speed of sound, then separated again. When could you study the opponent's stance properly? Only that instant inside sword range. For the uncanny sword to do its work, no room.

But add something outside ordinary limits, and the matter changed.

Outside ordinary limits—◆those eyes.

Haan. Even from this distance, the enemy knew exactly what I was doing.

Too clearly it could see.
Those terrifying eyes could see this sword.

Then?
ja:
太刀はひたりと、前方へ。

　敵騎の矢を迎える我もまた一筋の矢と化す。

　鋭き尖鋒を備えた刺貫の一器。

　この技は大鳥獅子吼から学び取った。
　眩惑の剣――尖端で相手の視界焦点を刺し、精神と
感覚の平衡を失わしめる妖術。

　……無論、俺とてわかっている。
　あの技は至近距離の白兵戦であったからこそ効果を
上げたのだ。

　遠距離から音速で接敵しまた遠く離れる、空の武者
戦にあって、相手の戦形かまえを詳細に観察できる機会など
太刀打間合クロスレンジへ入るほんの一刹那しかない。
　妖剣の働く余地は無かった。

　しかしここに、常識外の要素が加われば話は変わる。
　常識外の――◆あの眼が。

　そう。
　敵はこの遠距離で、精確にこちらの動静を掌握して
いる……。

　見えてしまっているのだ・・・・・・・・・・・。
　恐るべき凶瞳には、この剣が。

　ならば？

en:
The dazzling might not hold for even a moment or two.
Just now, that was eternity.

The enemy would shoot before its senses recovered. Wait, and I would reach it. First strike gone. So it had to shoot.

While dazzled, how to aim?

...One way only.
ja:
眩惑効果は一瞬も二瞬も保もたないだろう。
　しかし今、それは永遠と等しい。

　敵は感覚の回復を待たずに撃つ。
　待っていては俺に接敵され、先制の機を失う以上、
そうする以外に無いのだ。

　眩惑されながら、如何にして狙点を定めるか？

　……方法は唯一つだ。

en:
Yes.
Only the sword point was visible? Aim at the sword point.

The opponent—me—was there. That would do. With the shot aimed exactly at me, I would have to dodge, unless I attempted the madness of cutting it aside.

That second possibility could be dismissed. Once I dodged, the sword point's spell would release the enemy. Then its Divine Art could work freely.

The shot would bend. From some impossible angle it would pierce me.
The end.

Its decision was correct.
Absolutely correct.◆

The mistake had come earlier.

It should have fired at once. Do not give me that one second to make a plan! Rough aim, anything would do. The Divine Art could correct the shot afterward. At the moment of firing, an inaccurate aim was no problem.

But perhaps the archer's pride would not permit such sloppy work. A little time it had spent taking proper aim.

There. The mistake.

Only one mistake. Enough to kill the bow knight.
ja:
そう。
　剣先しか見えないなら、その剣先を狙って撃つ・・・・・・・・・・。

　そこに対手おれはいるのだから、それで良い。
　正確に狙われた俺は、無謀にもそれを切り払おうと
するのでなければ、回避しなくてはならない。

　前者は考慮から外して良いだろう。
　俺が回避動作をとったなら――俺の剣先の呪縛から
解き放たれたなら。敵騎はあの陰義の威力を遺憾なく
発揮する事ができる。

　射撃は屈曲し、有り得ない角度から俺を射抜く。
　それで結末ジ・エンドだ。

　だから敵の決断は正しい。
　全く間違っていない。◆

　間違いは、その前の段階において存在した。

　敵は俺に作戦を考える一秒間など与えず、さっさと
撃っておくべきだったのだ。
　照準など適当でいい。どうせ陰義で修正が利くのだ
から。発射時点の照準が外れていても問題はなかった。

　しかし、射手のプライドがそんな雑な射撃を許さな
かったのか……。
　敵は照準を合わせるため、僅かな時間を費やした。

　誤りは其処。
　ただ一つの失敗が、弓騎士を殺す。

en: Kanae"————Ah————"

Dodge? No.
Cut the arrow aside? No.

To the approaching arrow, no reaction at all.

Because I trusted the archer.
The marksman of that magic shot, I trusted completely.

Miss, it would not. Even that single point at the tip of my sword.

No need to dodge. No need to defend. Just keep going straight.

The enemy would hit my sword for me. Without fail!
ja:
回避、しない。
　切り払いもしない。

　迫り来る矢に対して、一切の反応リアクションを起こさない。

　何故なら俺は信じている。
　魔弾の射手を信じている。

　絶対に外さない、と。
　太刀の尖端の一点さえ。

　避ける必要も防ぐ必要もない。
　真っ直ぐに進み続けるだけでいい。

　敵は必ず、俺の剣に当ててくれる！

en:
The sword twisted, broke, shattered.
My right arm went with it.

But life remained. Strength enough to move, one scraping of it, remained.

Enough. This much would do.
To that last drop I entrusted everything.

Forward.
One more step. Then the step after that.
ja:
太刀が拗ねじけて、折れて、砕けた。
　右腕までも吹き飛んだ。

　しかしまだ命は残っている。
　削り滓かすほどだが、動く力が残されている。

　足りる。
　その一滴の力に全て託そう。

　進むのだ。
　あと一歩。その先のあと一歩を。

en:
With my left hand, I drew the wakizashi.
My final weapon.

The enemy had drawn its sword also.
ja:
左手で脇差を抜く。
　最後の武器。

　敵もまた剣を抜いていた。

en:
Had I cut it?
Had it cut me?

...I no longer knew.
ja:
斬ったのか。
　斬られたのか。

　……それはもう、わからなかった。

en:
I walked the forest path.

The body was heavy. So very heavy.
This piece gone, that piece gone, and still heavier than usual. How was that?

Still I walked.
Walk I must.
ja:
森の道を歩く。

　身体はとてもとても重い。
　あれやこれや欠けてしまったのに、どうしてか普段
より重かった。

　それでも歩く。
　歩かなくてはいけないのだ。

en: Muramasa《...Mido...》Kageaki"Muramasa..."Muramasa《I am sorry. For me... this seems to be as far as I go...》Kageaki"Yes..."
ja:
村正《……御堂……》景明「村正……」村正《ごめんなさい。
　私は……ここまで、みたい……》景明「ああ……」

en:
My faithful partner—my friend—seemed to be going ahead.

Even turn my head and see her off, that much strength I did not have. One breath I squeezed out. To say the last thing that had to be said. That much only.
ja:
忠実でいてくれた相棒ともは、先にゆくようだ。

　そちらへ首を傾けて、見送ってやる余力すらない。
　一息を搾り出して、最後に伝えるべき事を伝えるの
が精一杯だった。

en: Kageaki"Thank you."Muramasa《............》
ja: 景明「ありがとう」村正《…………》

en:
Alone now.
Along the forest path I walked.

Hard going. Heavy body, thin consciousness. When had everything become so terribly cold?

It hurt.
Life was running out.

The heart wanted to stop. I kept forcing it to work, kept trying to live. That was why it hurt. Stop this foolish business, and surely the pain would finish at once.

But not yet.
Until I reached her, dying was not permitted.
ja:
独りきり。
　森の道を歩く。

　辛かった。
　身体は重く、意識は薄く、辺りはいつしか酷く寒い。

　苦しい。
　命が尽きかけているからだ。

　止まりそうな心臓を無理に動かして、生き続けよう
としているから苦しいのだ。
　馬鹿なことをやめれば、きっと苦痛はすぐに終わる。

　けれどまだ、俺は死んではならないのだ。
　彼女のもとへ帰りつくまでは。

en:
...When I became aware again, I was lying on the ground.
My legs seemed to have exhausted their strength.

They would no longer move.
ja:
……気付くと、倒れ伏していた。
　脚の力が尽きたらしい。

　もう動かない。

en: Kageaki(No.)
ja: 景明（駄目だ）

en:
I must get up.

I must not die yet.

Not yet. Not here. I did not want to die.
ja:
立ち上がらなくては。

　まだ死んではならない。

　まだ、ここでは、死にたくない。

en: Kageaki(Surely... all of them—)
ja: 景明（きっと……誰もが）

en:
Had thought so.

The people I had killed. At the moment I killed them.

They had cried that they did not want to die.
Not yet. They did not want to die yet.

I had trampled that desperate plea.
ja:
そう思ったのだ。
　俺が殺してきた人々は。俺に殺されるその瞬間。

　死にたくない。
　まだ死にたくないと、叫んだのだ。

　俺はその悲痛な願いを踏みにじった。

en: Kageaki(So—)
ja: 景明（だから）

en:
So.
I must not die here.
ja:
だから・・・。
　俺は、ここで死んではならないのだ。

en:
Strength I did not have, I summoned. Lifted myself. Teeth clenched, one remaining arm braced against the ground.

Stand.
Live.

Only a little more. Until I reached her.
Kanae Ootori.

She was an avenger. The one who would judge Kageaki Minato's crimes. The person who would give him his rightful death.

My life had to be offered to her blade. She would take it on account of the unappeased grief of someone I had killed.

She would show the anger of good against evil.

Justice existed in this world.
Evil would certainly receive its due.

This I believed.
This I wanted to believe.

So this life must end by her hand.
ja:
無い力を奮って、身体を起こす。
　歯を食い縛って、隻腕を立てる。

　立たねば。
　生きねば。

　あと少し。
　彼女のもとにゆくまで。

　大鳥香奈枝のもとへ。

　彼女は復讐者。
　湊斗景明の罪を裁くもの。

　湊斗景明に正しい死を与えてくれる人。

　俺の命は彼女の刃に捧げられなくてはならない。
　彼女は、俺に殺された人の無念にかけて、俺の命を
奪うのだから。

　悪に対する善の怒りを示してくれるから。

　この世に正義はある。
　悪に対する報いは、必ずある。

　そう信じる。
　信じたい。

　だからこの命は彼女の手で。

en: Kageaki(...Ah...)
ja: 景明（……あぁ）

en:
She was there.
There.

She had come.

Kanae Ootori.
ja:
いる。
　そこに、いる。

　来てくれた。

　大鳥香奈枝。

en: Kageaki(Captain.)
ja: 景明（大尉）

en:
I conveyed my hope.
—Judgment. Condemnation.

Whether a voice came out, I did not know. But I felt no anxiety.

She was a pure executor of vengeance. It would be all right.

I trusted her.

Kanae Ootori's personality was probably complicated. My understanding of it was not deep. So much I surely did not know.

Perhaps she possessed an appalling nature utterly opposed to human morality. Perhaps she was a demon with a human face and a beast's heart.

Looking back, there had certainly been glimpses to suggest it.

...But what did it matter to me?

Nothing. So I had not troubled myself with it.
ja:
希望を伝える。
　――裁きを。断罪を。

　声が出たかどうか、わからない。
　だが不安は抱かなかった。

　彼女は純正の復讐執行者。
　だから、大丈夫。

　信じている。

　大鳥香奈枝という人の、おそらく複雑であったのだ
ろう人格について、俺の理解は必ずしも深くなかった。
　きっと知らないことは数多ある。

　もしかしたら彼女は、人倫に全く反するおぞましき
性質の所有者であったのかもしれない。
　人面獣心の化生けしょうであったのかもしれない。

　そう思わせる片鱗は、顧みれば確かにあった。

　……だが、そんなことはどうでも構わなかったのだ。

　どうでも構わなかったから、気にも留めなかった。

en:
She had promised vengeance for Kageaki Minato's crimes.

Firmly.
Mercilessly.
Never would she pardon him.

That was everything.
For me, that was enough.

So I could say this.

This woman, perhaps a devil strayed into the human world, was no different to Kageaki Minato from a messenger of heaven.

Kanae Ootori.
My gratitude to you.

The gratitude of my whole being.
ja:
彼女は湊斗景明の罪に復讐を約束してくれた。

　固く。
　無慈悲に。
　決して、赦ゆるしはしないと。

　それが全てだった。

　俺にはそれだけで良かった。

　だから云える。

　人の世界に迷い込んだ悪魔であったのかもしれない
この女性ひとは、
　湊斗景明にとって、天の使いと何一つ違うところが
なかったと。

　大鳥香奈枝。
　貴方に感謝を。

　全身全霊の感謝を。

en:
Something warm touched my neck.

Was this... the blade————

The last remnant of life melted and vanished. At last I was given the death I sought.

The death of condemnation.
ja:
温かい何かが、首に触れる。

　これが……刃か――――

　生命の最後の片鱗が、溶けて消えた。
　求める死は遂に、俺に与えられた。

　断罪の死。

en: Kageaki(...And yet—)
ja: 景明（……なのに）

en:
One last thing.
One small complaint my soul had kept.

No suffering.
No pain either.

Only soft. Only kind.

On this point I was dissatisfied.

...For Kageaki Minato, death ought to have been much harsher.
ja:
最後に一つ。
　俺の魂は、小さな不満を残した。

　苦しくない。
　痛くもない。

　ただ柔らかくて、優しかった。

　だからそれが、不服だった。

　……湊斗景明に与えられる死は、もっと苛酷なもの
でなくてはならないのに。

en:
She looked down at his lifeless face.
...He seemed satisfied. But just a little dissatisfied also.

A sleeping face with something childlike about it. The uncharacteristic expression made her laugh.

She could no longer give the laugh a voice.
ja:
息絶えた彼の顔を見下ろす。
　……満足そうで。けれど少しだけ、不満そうだった。

　どこか子供っぽい寝顔。
　彼らしくない表情に、笑いがこぼれる。

　声を立てることは、もうできなかったけれど。

en: Kanae(Such a fool, you.)
ja: 香奈枝（ばかなひと）

en:
To the very end, he had never protected himself.

He could have fled. He should have understood that he did not need to die here.

Instead, he had stayed and fought. Probably with some thought of protecting Kanae also.

He had fought for the woman who swore to kill him.
Against that very woman he was trying to protect.

And died.

Such foolishness.
No helping it. No saving him from it. Such foolishness.
ja:
とうとう最後まで、自分自身を庇かばわなかった。

　逃げれば良かったのだ。
　俺はこんなところで死ななくても良いのだと、そう
気付くべきだったのだ。

　なのに彼は踏み留まって、戦った。
　おそらくは、香奈枝を守ろうという想いもあって。

　彼は自分を殺すと誓った女のために戦った。
　他でもない、守ろうとしたその女と。

　そして死んだ。

　まったく愚かしい。
　救いようもなく、どうしようもなく愚かしい。

en: Kanae(But—)
ja: 香奈枝（けれど）

en:
Which one was the bigger fool, though?

He fought Kanae to protect Kanae.
She hid the truth, made him do that, and had him kill her.

Well.
...Same only, perhaps.

Two hopeless fools killed each other. Both dead. Very successful arrangement.

Surely that was all.

Dying did not frighten her.
No complaint about it either.

Living meant dying.
Dying meant living.

Same meaning. Different words.

Life starts from zero, or life goes toward zero. Only that much difference. Between seeking death and seeking life, then, what essential difference was there?

No use getting stuck on so much wordplay. Live rightly as yourself, die rightly as yourself. That was enough.

And this end was undoubtedly right for Kanae Ootori.
For Kageaki Minato also.

Wholeheartedly they had lived.
Wholeheartedly they had died.

As Kanae Ootori.
As Kageaki Minato.

So she thought.
ja:
より愚かしいのは、どちらだったのだろう。

　香奈枝を守ろうとして香奈枝と戦った彼と。
　真実を隠し、彼をしてそうさせ、我が身を殺させた
香奈枝と。

　まぁ。
　……同じようなものか。

　救えぬ愚か者同士が殺し合った。
　そしてめでたく、どちらも死んだ。

　これはきっと、それだけのことだ。

　死にゆくことに、怖れはなかった。
　不平もなかった。

　生きるとは、死ぬということ。
　死ぬとは、生きるということ。

　意味は同じ。
　言葉が違うだけ。

　人生をゼロから発したものと見るか、ゼロへ向かう
ものと見るか、ただそれだけの違い。
　だから死を求めることと、生を求めることとの間に、
本質の差は何も無いのだ。

　そんな言葉遊び程度の違いに拘泥しても仕方ない。
　自己おのれとして正しく生きて、正しく死ぬなら、それで
良い。

　そしてこの最期は間違いなく、大鳥香奈枝にとって
正しい帰結。
　湊斗景明の最期もそう。

　直向ひたむきに生きた。
　直向に死んだ。

　大鳥香奈枝として。
　湊斗景明として。

　そう思う。

en: Kanae(Listen, na.)
ja: 香奈枝（ねぇ）

en:
She addressed him, though he would answer no more.

We were fools.
Such fools, really.

But this only we could do, no?
Another road we could not choose.

We met. We died together—
And this was the farce we made.

So foolish, so ridiculous. And nobody in the audience.
Only us two.
ja:
もう応えない彼に、語りかける。

　わたくしたち、愚かだったけれど。
　本当に、愚かだったけれど。

　こうするしかなかったものね。

　ほかの道は選べなかったものね。

　ふたり出会って、一緒に死んで――
　こうして出来た、道化芝居。

　こんなにも愚劣で、こんなにも滑稽なのに、観客は
誰もいない。
　わたくしたちはふたりきり。

en: Kanae(So, you see—)
ja: 香奈枝（だから、ね）

en:
This story is yours and mine only.

Come, let us laugh together.
Point at the clowns. At the foolish way they lived.
ja:
この物語はわたくしとあなただけのもの。

　ふたりきりで笑いましょう。
　道化たちを指差して。その愚かしい生き様を。

en:
Step by step, I walked back to my residence—the detention centre.

Killing that journalist, so ready to stand up for others, weighed on both shoulders.

Guilt. A load you cannot throw away somewhere, cannot leave with somebody else.

Keep living, and the load keeps growing. That is why people live rightly: to make it even a little lighter.

And here was I, taking on murder after murder, the heaviest crime. As though I wanted to show off how much weight my mind could carry.

Aur lao. Bring some more. Shoulders still attached? Then apparently the capacity had not been reached. Such a magnificent strongman, Kageaki Minato: his great feat was continuing to walk while other people supplied the dead weight.

All for one private desire. Stop the Silver Star. My sister.

...A fool, then.
Probably a fool of the worst kind.

Not even worth laughing at.
Spit on him. What else could one do with such a fool?

Samajh bhi raha hai. He understands all this. Carries on anyway.
There was the hopeless part.
ja:
拘置所すまいへの道を、ぽつぽつと歩く。

　義侠心溢れるジャーナリストを殺めた行為は両肩に
重かった。
　罪――何処かへ捨てることも、誰かに預けることも、
決して叶わない荷。

　生き続ける限りそれは積み重ねられ続ける。だから
こそ人は正しく生きて少しでも荷を減らすのだ。
　が、この俺はあたかも精神の剛力を誇示するが如く、
殺人という最大の罪を次から次へと抱え込んでいる。

　銀星号いもうとを止める、その自己一身の欲求のためだけに。

　……俺は愚かなのだろう。
　おそらく、最も質たちの悪い意味で愚かなのだ。

　嘲笑うにも値しない。
　唾棄する以外に仕様もない、愚物。

　そうと自覚してなお続ける、救いの無さ。

en: Muramasa《...Mido.》Kageaki"............"Muramasa《I have said it before. Again and again. You do not have to think about anything.》Muramasa《Just let me use you. Switch your mind off. If you cannot... hate me instead.》Muramasa《...But yourself... please stop hating yourself...》Kageaki"And my answer? That also I have given, again and again."Muramasa《...》Kageaki"You are a tsurugi. A tool. Something to be used, nothing more."Kageaki"A tool does what the user makes it do. How is it to carry guilt? The human using it carries that."Kageaki"Only the human deserves hatred. That is me. Know your place, tool."Muramasa《............》
ja:
村正《……御堂》景明「…………」村正《繰り返し、言ってきたことだけれどね。
　貴方は何も考えなくていい》村正《私に使われていればいい。心を止めて。
　止められないなら……私を憎めばいい》村正《……自分を憎むのはやめて……》景明「俺の答えも、繰り返し言ってきた」村正《……》景明「劒冑おまえは道具だ。
　使われるものに過ぎない」景明「使われるだけの道具は罪など背負えない。
　使う人間が罪を背負う」景明「憎悪に値するのは人間おれのみだ。
　分際を知れ、道具」村正《…………》

en:
How many times had we had this conversation? Ever since I bonded with Muramasa, two years ago.

Sometimes she began it. Sometimes I did. But the result never changed. Both went silent. Neither gave way. Conversation finished.

I would not yield because this was precisely where I could not yield. For Muramasa, probably the same.

So the conversation could only end in mutual refusal, producing nothing.◆

Until now, that was how it went.
ja:
同様の対話を幾度交わしたろう。
　二年前のあの時、村正と結縁してから。

　今のように村正が言い出すこともあれば、俺の側が
口火を切ることもあった。
　然しかして結末は毎回変わらず。二人共に黙り込んで、
互いに譲らないまま話を終える。

　俺が譲らないのは、それが譲れない部分だからだ。
　村正にとっても、同じなのだろう。

　だから対話はいつも不毛に、相互の拒絶で終結する
ほかない。◆

　これまでは、そうだった。

en: Kageaki"But."Muramasa《...What?》Kageaki"————"
ja: 景明「だが」村正《……えっ？》景明「――――」

en:
One word of objection had come out without warning.
And the words that were to follow it—◆those had not troubled to arrive in my conscious mind.



I shut my mouth again and walked. Muramasa followed, hidden in the night.

But the tsurugi's silence had a question in it. Naturally. Suddenly break the established routine, and she was entitled to wonder.

I was wondering myself. In that one strange instant, what had I thought? What had I meant to insist on?

But.

After that word, what?

Already I had let it go. It lay at the bottom of the swamp in my mind, where I could neither see it nor reach it. Eventually it would dissolve and disappear.

And what would be wrong with that? Nothing, surely.
Yet for some reason, there was a thread in my mind, and I was pulling at it.

A thread joined to something at the bottom of that swamp.
ja:
不意に口をついて出た、逆接の一語。
　そして続けるべき言葉は――◆しかし、俺の意識野に
存在していなかった。


　元通りに口を噤んで、歩く。
　村正も、夜陰に潜んで従ついてくる。

　が、劒冑の沈黙は、物問いたげな成分を含んでいた。
　それはそうだ。やにわに約束事パターンを崩されれば、疑問
も湧くだろう。

　俺自身さえ不思議だった。
　魔が差したかのような一刹那、俺は何を思い、何と
言い募ろうとしたのか。

〝だが〟

　その言葉の後に、何を。

　既に手放してしまったそれは、もう俺の精神の沼の
底だ。見えないし、手に取ることもできない。
　やがては完全に溶けて、消えてしまうだろう。

　そうなって、何が不味いということも無かろうに。
　俺はどうしてか、脳裏で糸・を手繰たぐっていた。

　沼の底の何かと繋がっている糸を。

en:
...Call that thread a scene.
Only, it was not rooted in me.

Images that had passed through my mind while Aoe held me in his world of illusion. Probably his Divine Art had drawn them out too—from somewhere other than my mind.

Foreign images. They fitted neither my dreams nor my past. Apparently I had forgotten them the very instant I saw them.

...Somehow, now I was getting them back.

I knew I had seen them. Knew I had forgotten them once. And now their contents were returning.

In pieces, yes.
But I could show them on the mirror inside my mind.

Those—◆

Muramasa's memories.
ja:
……言うなれば、その糸は情景だった。
　但し、俺自身に根差すものとは違う。

　青江の幻覚世界に囚われている最中さなか、意識野を通り
抜けていった光陰。
　あれもやはり、青江の陰義で引き出されたものだっ
たのだろう。俺の心ではない処から。

　俺の夢、俺の過去に符合しない異質なそれを、俺は
見た瞬間に忘却してしまったらしい。

　……どういう次第でか、今の・・俺は取り戻している。

　確かに見たことを、一度忘れ去ったことをも自覚し、
そして内容を思い出している。

　断片的にだが。
　心裡の鏡面へ映し出せる。

　それを――――◆

　村正の、記憶を。

en:
This is not the story of a hero.

We cannot all remain heroes.
ja:
これは英雄の物語ではない。

　誰もが英雄ではいられない。

en: Even so, everyone keeps fighting.
ja: それでも誰もが戦っている。

en:
In the sky, on the ground—war.

Blood washing away blood. Mountains of corpses. For once, the expression was not making any exaggeration.

Below, archers shot gaps into the enemy lines. Through them came men in masses, long weapons together, mounted commanders leading. Above, warriors picked worthy opponents, announced their names, split clouds and rode the wind into fierce sword exchanges.

War.
From the age called medieval.

Look more closely, and the period could be narrowed down. Tsurugi shapes, styles of combat, the infantry's weapons and dress. Neither the Genpei War nor the struggles of the Sengoku lords fitted these things.

Above all, the banners.
Rich brocade. Gold sun, red field.

Both sides had them.

Even in Yamato's history, not many times had this arrangement occurred. Not many wars.
ja:
天と地で、争いが繰り広げられていた。
　血で血を洗う――屍山を築くという表現がまさしく
相応しい。

　地上では、射手が矢を射かけ、敵陣に間隙を穿つや、
騎馬の将帥率いる兵の群れが長物を連ねて押し進む。
　天空では、互いを好敵と見定めた武者同士が名乗り
合い、雲を裂き風に乗って、激しく太刀を打ち交わす。

　戦争の光景だ。
　中世……そう呼ばれる時代の。

　詳細に観察すれば、より正確な区分も可能だった。
　劒冑の形状、武者の戦闘形式、歩兵の武器装束――
それらはこの戦争が源平合戦でも戦国大名の抗争でも
ないことを如実に語っている。

　何よりも、戦場に散見する旗……
　赤地に金で日輪を描いた豪奢な錦織。

　それが、どちらの陣営にも存在する・・・・・・・・・・・・。
　そんな事態、そんな戦争が起きた時代は、大和史上
にも稀であった。

en: Muramasa II"Father."
ja: 二世村正「御父おと」

en: At the voice beside me, my head turned of itself.
ja: 傍らの声に、俺の首が独りでにそちらへ向く。

en:
A small Emishi woman.

From beside her, I looked up at her face.
Up. Meaning, I was shorter than even she was.

But she was not calling me.
Her voice went to the back of the man standing ahead.
ja:
小柄な蝦夷の女性だった。
　その顔を隣から見上げる――見上げている。つまり
俺の背は彼女よりも低かった。

　彼女が声を投じたのは俺にではない。
　前方に立つ、男の背へ向けていた。

en: Muramasa I"Can you see which way it is going?"Muramasa II"Our side will lose, it seems."Muramasa I"Haan. ...Sasaki, that bloody turncoat. Again his special talent is on display."
ja:
始祖村正「流れが、見えたか」二世村正「吾あが方の負けであろう」始祖村正「そうさな。
　……佐々木めがまたしても得意の寝返りを
打ちおった」

en:
The man's voice was bitter. Hearing it, I noticed also.

One force had turned its weapons around and was attacking those who had been its comrades moments before...
ja:
忌々しげな男の声。
　それを聞いて、俺も気付いた。

　一隊が鉾の向きを逆さにし、先刻までの仲間に攻め
掛かっている……。

en: Muramasa I"Nothing to be done now."Muramasa II"Even Akima saab seems unable to hold them."Muramasa I"..."Muramasa II"So all that loyal heart cannot beat one expert backstabber, then?"Muramasa I"No such thing!"Muramasa II"He is losing in front of us..."Muramasa I"For now only! The sovereign we serve in Yoshino is the rightful Emperor. The fellow sitting in Kyoto has noble blood, haan, but a pretender he remains."Muramasa I"In the end, the righteous win. The world is made that way."Muramasa II"..."Muramasa I"You cannot believe it?"Muramasa II"I cannot."Muramasa I"You must."Muramasa II"Heaven to earth, Father, only you I trust."Muramasa I"..."Muramasa II"The forging you taught me, that I trust. The perfection of tsurugi you are still to discover, that also I shall trust."Muramasa II"Then I shall take your place. That only I believe is my work appointed by heaven."Muramasa I"...I see."Muramasa II"Let us go home, Father. The battle is over."Muramasa I"Yes..."Muramasa"Over?"
ja:
始祖村正「どうにもならぬ」二世村正「飽間あきま様も、支え切れぬようだ」始祖村正「……」二世村正「あの方の赤心忠義も、佐々木の裏切り根性
には敵わぬか」始祖村正「左様なことはない！」二世村正「現に敗れている……」始祖村正「一時の事だ。
　うてらが奉ずる吉野の主上こそ正当の帝、
いま京に御座すは尊き血筋ではあれど僭帝に
過ぎぬ」始祖村正「最後には正しき者が勝つ。
　世は、そう出来ている」二世村正「……」始祖村正「信じられぬか」二世村正「信じられぬ」始祖村正「信じねばならぬ」二世村正「吾あれが信ずるは、天上天下に御父のみよ」始祖村正「……」二世村正「御父に教えられた鍛冶の技を信じている。
　御父がこれから・・・・見つけ出す、劒冑の極みも
信じようぞ」二世村正「そうして、御父の跡を継ぐ。
　それだけが、吾の天命と思うている」始祖村正「……そうか」二世村正「帰ろう、御父。
　戦は終わりだ」始祖村正「うむ……」村正「おわり？」

en:
Suddenly, I had spoken.
In a voice that was not mine.

Hearing a strange voice emerge from my own body...

Yet the sensation was familiar. Every time I donned armour, I experienced it.

Only this voice was a little younger than usual.
ja:
不意に、俺は・・声を発した。
　俺のものではない声で。

　我が身から生じる異質な声を聴く……

　それはしかし、良く慣れ親しんだ感覚だった。

　装甲する都度、これと同じ体験をしている。
　ただ今の声は、いつもと比べると、些いささか幼かった。

en: Muramasa"Maa. Is the war over? No more fighting?"Muramasa II"..."Muramasa I"..."
ja:
村正「かかさま。いくさ、おわったの？
　もう、やらない？」二世村正「……」始祖村正「……」

en:
Even to an outsider like me, the difference in meaning was clear. The owner of that young voice—someone I knew very well—had misunderstood their conversation.

The woman shook her head slightly.
ja:
ニュアンスの齟齬は、部外者である俺の耳にも明白
だった。
　幼い声の主――俺の良く知る者――は、二人の会話
を誤解している。

　女性の方が、小さく首を振った。

en: Muramasa II"Not yet. It will go on."Muramasa"Until when?"Muramasa II"I do not know."Muramasa"...When did the war start?"Muramasa II"Long before you were born."Muramasa"Before I was born?"Muramasa II"Yes."Muramasa"And you, Maa? When you were born?"Muramasa"Was there no war?"Muramasa II"...There was."Muramasa"And Nana?"Muramasa I"..."Muramasa"When you were born, Nana? Was there no war?"Muramasa I"..."Muramasa I"There was."
ja:
二世村正「まだだ。
　まだ、続く」村正「いつまで？」二世村正「わからぬ」村正「……いくさは、いつからしてるの？」二世村正「なれの生まれる前から、ずっとだ」村正「あてのうまれるまえ？」二世村正「そうだ」村正「かかさまは？
　かかさまのうまれたころは？」村正「いくさ、なかった？」二世村正「……あった」村正「じじさまは？」始祖村正「……」村正「じじさまのうまれたころは？
　いくさ、なかった？」始祖村正「……」始祖村正「あったよ」

en:
The storm of war was said to have raged across all Yamato for a hundred years.

The conflict of the Northern and Southern Courts.

The world my tsurugi—Muramasa—had lived in.
ja:
その戦嵐は、百年に渡って大和全土を吹き荒れたと
伝えられている。

　南北朝争乱。

　俺の劒冑――村正が、生きていた世界。

en: Muramasa II"Father. Akima saab is here."Muramasa I"Ah."
ja:
二世村正「御父。
　飽間様がお越しだ」始祖村正「おう」

en:
A simple house in a backcountry Emishi village.

The visitor had the bearing of a formidable warrior. Surely a commander with a district and an army in his charge. Between such a man and an ordinary Emishi, the difference in station ought to be earth and sky.

The householder did not even stand.
A proper greeting? That also, no.

And the warrior took no offence.
...Achha. Was that the sort of relationship?

Earth and sky, certainly. But the sky had come to visit, and the earth could not be bothered to get up. All my understanding of rank was standing there very properly, waiting for somebody to be offended. Neither man obliged. Between friends, apparently, even the social order could be told: shoes off, sit quietly.
ja:
鄙ひなびた蝦夷村の素朴な屋敷。
　そこに現れたのは、堂々たる風情の武人だった。

　一郡一軍を預かる将領に違いない。
　一介の蝦夷とは天と地ほどの身分差がある……筈だ
が、家主は立ち上がりもせず、挨拶らしき挨拶もしな
かった。

　武人に、それを不快がる気色はない。
　……そういう間柄なのか。

en: Muramasa I"You are safe. That is what matters."Akima"You were watching?"Muramasa I"Yes."Akima"Sasaki, what a fellow. Time and place for betrayal, never once does he get those wrong."Akima"At least a rank or two the Yoshino people could have given generously. His complaints they kept waving away. Now see."Muramasa I"Such profit-eating fellows, who needs them? If he is going to change sides anyway, put him on the enemy side from the beginning. Less confusion."Akima"...His own logic he follows, though. Land he wants, rank he wants. North to south, south to north, full running about. All to protect his clan."Muramasa I"Whole thing ulta! A commander uses his clan's strength to protect the greater cause."Muramasa I"Throw away the cause to protect the clan, and still call yourself a warrior? On what basis?"Akima"Yes..."Muramasa I"You would not change to the Northern Court, Akima saab, even if every last member of your clan and following were to die."Akima"Naturally not."Muramasa I"This province of Ise lies at the Grand Shrine's feet. Nowhere do the people revere the Emperor more strongly, or hate rebels more deeply."Muramasa I"To a false emperor, our heads will not bend. Bilkul nahin."Akima"Yes."Muramasa I"We must win..."Akima"For that, Muramasa, your strength is needed."Muramasa I"..."Akima"His Majesty says nothing, but he seems to be waiting impatiently. Kusunoki also."Muramasa I"Yes..."
ja:
始祖村正「無事で、何よりだ」飽間「見ていたか」始祖村正「うむ」飽間「佐々木も大した奴よ。
　裏切る時と場所を決して間違えん」飽間「吉野山の方々は位階くらい気前良くくれて
やるべきだった。
　奴の訴えを聞き流していたばかりに、この
ざまだ」始祖村正「欲得ずくの輩など要るまい。
　どうせ寝返る男なら、最初から敵に回して
おいた方がましだ」飽間「……あれはあれで筋は通しているがな。
　領地を求め官位を求め、北から南南から北
へと忙しく立ち回るのも、一族を守るためだ」始祖村正「本末転倒であろう。
　将ならば、大義を守護するために一族の力
を用いるべき」始祖村正「一族を守るために大義を捨てて、何の武人
か」飽間「うむ……」始祖村正「飽間様は、たとえ一族郎党悉く死に絶える
始末となろうが、北朝方へ鞍替えなどなさる
まい」飽間「当然だ」始祖村正「この伊勢國は神宮の膝元。
　民が帝を崇め、逆賊を憎む気持ちは、どの
國よりも強い」始祖村正「断じて偽帝に頭は下げられぬ」飽間「うむ」始祖村正「勝たねばならぬ……」飽間「そのためには、だ。
　村正。ぬしの力が要る」始祖村正「……」飽間「口にはされぬが、帝は待ちかねておられる
ようだ。
　楠木殿もな」始祖村正「うむ……」

en: Akima"The head smith of Sengo village, Kuwana, in Ise—Gorou Masamune come again, they said. His Majesty heard it. The imperial command came: forge a tsurugi. Three years now."Akima"Still not ready?"Muramasa I"Not yet."Akima"Put Kusunoki in your tsurugi and send him out at the head of the whole Southern army: the Northern Court would vanish in a single night."Akima"The peace Yamato's people have been waiting for would come at last..."Muramasa I"I also believe it must be so. That is exactly why I cannot just pick up the hammer and begin."Muramasa I"No second try is waiting for me..."Akima"Still unable to devise it?"Muramasa I"More a matter of direction."Akima"Direction?"Muramasa I"Akima saab, what do you consider the supreme tsurugi?"Akima"Great strength, hard armour, wings swift and sharp—"Muramasa I"And this thing can actually be made, you think?"Akima"...No."Muramasa I"However clever the smith, he cannot hammer out 'everything, please.' One thing you choose, another you give up. It has to be done."Akima"And you cannot settle the choice?"Muramasa I"Yes."Akima"What is best, what is supreme... is that the question?"Muramasa I"The supreme tsurugi, Akima saab? The one that does its work. That is all."Muramasa I"Who must it help? Who must it destroy? ...First make that clear. Otherwise nothing begins."Akima"The Southern Court is our ally, the Northern Court our enemy, surely?"Muramasa I"More deeply. More exactly. Purpose clear, abilities can be made more specialised. The clearer the work, the better I can shape the tsurugi for it."

en: Akima"...I see."Muramasa I"First know the purpose. Then decide the working. Bas, that is the matter."Akima"Hence the visits to battlefields."Muramasa I"Yes."Akima"Will you arrive at a conclusion?"Muramasa I"It will take more time. I still cannot see the enemy that must be defeated."Muramasa I"Some turncoat like Sasaki is not enough."Akima"I see... Very well. I shall let Kusunoki know your thinking, discreetly."Akima"It will reach His Majesty also. Both should understand."Muramasa I"I am sorry."Akima"Arre, between you and me, what need for such distant words?"Akima"You keep thinking, to your heart's content. Till then, these rebel armies I shall keep out of Yoshino."Muramasa I"...I leave it to you."

en: Muramasa"Welcome, Akima saab."Akima"Arre, I almost did not recognise you! These Emishi children, a man blinks once and there is more child than before."Akima"If I don't pay attention, Muramasa's daughter and granddaughter will get exchanged in my head."Muramasa II"...Bas, now you are overdoing it. This one is still a child."Muramasa II"In forging also, the foundations are only just coming. Whether even those have come properly is another question."Muramasa"But height-wise I have passed Maa. A little."Muramasa II"Hm."Muramasa I's Wife"Heh..."Muramasa I"I hear you have spent a long time fighting from place to place."Akima"Haan. It was not for nothing. That rat Akamatsu's betrayal sent us downhill; at last we have climbed about halfway back."Akima"The late Emperor had to leave this world a prisoner. Perhaps a little of his bitterness we have settled, no? Your son-in-law's also..."Muramasa II"..."Muramasa"..."Muramasa I"...And this gentleman?"Akima"Ah. A scholar-monk from Mount Kurama."

en: Uramu"I am Uramu. I hope we shall get along."Muramasa I"..."Akima"Learning-wise, this man goes very deep. For a long time he has been something like the Southern Court's behind-the-scenes adviser."Muramasa I"Oh..."Akima"Myself, I have troubled him any number of times. The other day also I took a problem to him, and your name happened to come up—"Uramu"You are seeking the supreme tsurugi, I am told. This proposition is very interesting. Very, very interesting."Uramu"Please let me help."Akima"—So he said."Muramasa I"Help? ...Forging you know?"Uramu"No. Forging I do not know. But the world I have travelled is wide. Very wide."Uramu"I know many branches of learning. I have seen many tsurugi also."Muramasa I"...Hm."Akima"So? Going by that, the tsurugi idea is still refusing to come together, no?"Akima"Try borrowing Uramu ji's brains. Your own will not get confiscated."Muramasa I"Well... Put like that, I have no particular objection to produce."Muramasa I"As you can see, ours is a poor village. For a man used to Kyoto, inconvenience will be available in abundance... Even so, you are willing?"Uramu"It is. Thank you, Muramasa ji."Uramu"I hope we shall work well together."Muramasa I"..."

en: Uramu"Muramasa ji, are you good at calculation?"Muramasa I"...What a question. Calculation I cannot do, but tsurugi I am forging? How will that arrangement work?"Uramu"Then please answer. Add seventy-eight thousand four hundred twenty-one to six hundred twenty-five thousand five hundred ninety-two. Subtract one hundred fifty-six thousand fifty-nine. Then multiply by three. What do you obtain?"Muramasa I"............One moment. Let me get my counting rods—"Uramu"Hehehe. Even with the rods, a little time will be required, no?"Muramasa I"Little only."Uramu"Please try using these."

en: Muramasa I"...What are these? They look like some kind of symbols."Uramu"Numerals from India."Muramasa I"Numerals? These?"Uramu"Yes. This is one, this is two, this is three..."Muramasa I"Hm... Then the round symbol is ten."Uramu"No, it is not. That is zero."Muramasa I"Zero?"Uramu"It signifies that there is nothing. The numeral for an empty place is 0."Muramasa I"? ...?"Muramasa I"Nothing is there, toh why must I do the work of putting a number for it? Even nothing is giving me work now?"Uramu"..."Muramasa II"Ah—!?"Muramasa I"What is it?"Muramasa II"Arre, what 'what is it,' Baba! This is a bloody enormous discovery!!"Muramasa I"What?"Muramasa II"Uramu ji, to write ten with these numerals... would it look like this?"Uramu"Yes. Place 1 and 0 together. Beside each other, not one above the other, is the proper arrangement."Muramasa II"Baba, look here. Do that calculation with these numbers and—"

en: Muramasa II"Sixteen lakh forty-three thousand eight hundred sixty-two. Bas. Finished already..."Muramasa I"————"Uramu"You see? With India's numerals, the calculation becomes easier, no?"Muramasa I"No separate numerals for ten, hundred, thousand... Just ten symbols: one to nine, and 0. Every number expressed with them..."Muramasa I"Such a small trick, and this much calculation-work disappears!"Uramu"In fact, these numerals and this method reached Yamato long ago. Their shapes were a little different..."Uramu"But most people could not see the value. The ones who could, they made it their private property and hid it."Uramu"That is why it did not spread."Muramasa I"Hmm..."Uramu"Much other knowledge also made the whole journey across the sea, only to get buried here. And some has never been known here at all."Muramasa I"You know these things, Uramu ji?"Uramu"Yes."Muramasa I"...Teach me! No—this is a request I am making. Please teach me."Muramasa I"Please!"Uramu"No need to bow your head. I will teach you. For this only I have come."Uramu"To give you all my knowledge, Muramasa ji..."

en: Uramu"Muramasa ji. If the supreme tsurugi is what you want, the three primal energies—the three powers—you must know."Muramasa I"Three powers?"Uramu"The fundamental powers of this universe. I call them magnetic force, gravitational force and creative force."Muramasa I"............"Muramasa"Magnetic—as in a magnet?"Uramu"Yes. The power by which magnets attract and repel each other."Uramu"Do you understand the other two?"Muramasa I"No."Uramu"Every object has gravitational force. By this power, other objects it pulls toward itself."Muramasa I"...?"Uramu"I have picked up a stone. Now, if I let go, as you see—"Uramu"The stone falls to the ground."Muramasa I"..."Uramu"That is gravitational force."Muramasa"? ...?"Muramasa II"............"Muramasa II"Matlab—things fall because the earth's gravitational force is pulling them...?"Uramu"Yes. You are always quick to understand."Muramasa II"..."Muramasa I"...And creative force?"Uramu"The power that joins the basic elements together and builds objects."Muramasa I"Basic elements?"Uramu"Break an object into smaller and smaller pieces. Whatever remains at the end, which can be divided no further, we call a basic element."Uramu"The raw material of everything. Creative force puts it together in different combinations, and out come flowers, minerals, insects—and we ourselves."Muramasa I"That... is the work of gods and Buddhas?"Uramu"You may call it that."Muramasa I"...Creative force. And magnetic force... gravitational force...?"Uramu"Do not force the understanding. Anxiety and hurry, these two stand in the brain's way and then demand that it move faster."Uramu"In learning there is no shortcut. Slowly, we will learn."

en: Muramasa I"One thing I have been wanting to ask..."Uramu"Yes?"Muramasa I"Uramu ji, why are you interested in tsurugi?"Uramu"Does it seem strange?"Muramasa I"All creation's workings you have mastered, and still you are occupied with weapons... This part is not sitting properly in my head."Uramu"You honour me with the praise. But knowing-wise, I am still at nothing."Muramasa I"Surely not."Uramu"No. Nothing, truly. The thing I actually want to know, that is still very far away."Muramasa I"With all your knowledge also, still that far?"Uramu"I feel as though I am searching for one grain of gold dropped into the sea."Muramasa I"...Beyond my imagining."Uramu"Agape. God's love."Muramasa I"?"Uramu"I do not know where it is. Nor what shape it has..."Uramu"But this much I believe. Tsurugi are the wings given to human beings. The one way to reach heaven... In that case—"Uramu"Beyond perfecting them, what I am seeking must be there."Muramasa I"............"Uramu"Muramasa ji, our meeting was ordained. Shrinking from it is not possible. But..."Muramasa I"..."Muramasa II"Baba. Why are you not forging?"Muramasa II"Still unable to settle the design? But Uramu ji has already—"Uramu"Yes. All the knowledge I possess, I have given to Muramasa ji."Muramasa II"Sun liya? You heard him. Beyond all this, what more are you wanting?"Muramasa I"I cannot see."Muramasa II"...?"Muramasa I"It is not coming before me... The shape of the supreme tsurugi, still I cannot see it."Muramasa I"No. Now I am understanding even less than before."Muramasa II"Why?"Muramasa I"What is this tsurugi for...?"Muramasa I"What belief should go into the hammering? Kamine. Rotten rebels."Muramasa I"I cannot forgive them...!"Uramu"But the Southern Court is the same."Muramasa I"Wh-what!?"Uramu"Equally dirty work, they have done plenty. No—still more cowardly work also..."Muramasa I"Nonsense!"Uramu"It is true. The Southern Court's hidden work, I was often involved in it myself. So this I know very well."Uramu"Many people have been sacrificed to conspiracies. Most were powerless common people, guilty of nothing."Muramasa I"............"Muramasa I"Surely not... Impossible. Kusunoki and the others could not have done such things..."Uramu"The people at Yoshino are not bad people. They are all admirable."Uramu"But I told you before, no? The times themselves are bad."Uramu"A world where good people do evil things."Muramasa I"............"
ja:
浦夢「村正どの……」始祖村正「……浦夢殿か。
　傷に障る、もう休まれよ」浦夢「私は平気です。
　村正どのこそ、お体を大事に」浦夢「お酒の飲み過ぎ、体の毒です」始祖村正「…………」浦夢「北朝が、憎いですか」始祖村正「憎い……」始祖村正「何という……卑劣な……！
　外道め……賊どもめ」始祖村正「許せぬ……！」浦夢「けれど、南朝も同じです」始祖村正「な、何を!?」浦夢「同じくらい汚いこと、たくさんしてます。
　いえ、もっと卑怯なことも……」始祖村正「馬鹿なっ！」浦夢「本当です。
　私、南朝の陰の働きに関わること多かった
ので、良く知っています」浦夢「陰謀の犠牲になった人、とても多いです。
　そのほとんどは、何の罪もない、無力な民
たちでした」始祖村正「…………」始祖村正「まさか……有り得ぬ。
　楠木様たちが、そのような真似をなさる筈
が……」浦夢「吉野の方々、悪い人ではありません。
　皆、立派な方たちです」浦夢「けれど、前にも言いました。
　今は時代が悪いのです」浦夢「善き人々が、悪しき事をする世なのです」始祖村正「…………」

en: Muramasa I"Toh what am I supposed to do...?"Uramu"..."Muramasa I"Who is on my side, I don't know. Who is against me, that also I don't know."Muramasa I"What is right, I don't know. What is wrong, that also has gone from me."Muramasa I"What am I supposed to trust, then...!"Uramu"Muramasa ji..."Muramasa I"For what... am I... to forge a tsurugi...?"Uramu"..."Uramu"To put an evil world right... Is that not so?"Muramasa I"Arre, HOW to put it right! That is what I cannot see! Even the Southern Court's great cause I cannot trust now..."Uramu"Muramasa ji. Please listen carefully to what I am about to say."Uramu"Actually, one thing was still left for me to teach you. That I will tell you now."Muramasa I"...?"
ja:
始祖村正「では、うてはどうすれば良いのだ……」浦夢「……」始祖村正「誰が味方なのかわからぬ。
　誰が敵なのかもわからぬ」始祖村正「何が正しいのかわからぬ。
　何が誤りなのかもわからぬ」始祖村正「何を信じれば良いのかわからぬ……！」浦夢「村正どの……」始祖村正「うては……
　何のために……劒冑を打つのだ……」浦夢「……」浦夢「悪しき世を正すため……
　そうではないですか？」始祖村正「その道筋がわからんのだ！
　南朝の大義さえ信じられぬとあっては……」浦夢「村正どの。
　今からする話を、よく聞いてください」浦夢「あなたにお教えしなくてはならないこと、
実はあと一つ残っていました。
　それを、これからお話しします」始祖村正「……？」

en: Uramu"My true name... is Nicolas Flamel."Muramasa I"Nico...?"Uramu"Not coming easily to the tongue, no? Uramu is fine. The language where I was born and Yamato's language are completely different."Uramu"The two are very, very far apart."Muramasa I"...Were you from India, Uramu ji?"Uramu"No. Cross India and still you have very far to go."Muramasa I"From the Pure Land of the West...?"Uramu"West, yes... At the very end of the West. Pure Land, no."Uramu"Where I was born, war only, all the time. Same as Yamato now."Uramu"So I set out in search of a peaceful paradise."Muramasa I"..."Uramu"But such a country was not there anywhere. Every country: little peace, long fighting. Again little peace, again long fighting."Uramu"Finally I thought: instead of roaming about looking for a peaceful world, find how to make the world peaceful. And then... I met you."Muramasa I"...One ordinary smith I am. Now even my own way I have lost."Muramasa I"I can be of no help to you."Uramu"No. Precisely such a man as you is needed."Uramu"Tsurugi are the children of God... Consecrated beings in whom a fragment of miracle dwells."Uramu"Let the noblest tsurugi be born, and humanity's original sin will be washed away. God will forgive everybody. This earth itself he will make a paradise."Uramu"Yes... A righteous-hearted smith, swinging his hammer in search of truth—when that happens, this age of suffering must finish!"Muramasa I"...? Forgive me, I do not understand..."Muramasa I"Truth... is beyond me..."
ja:
浦夢「私の本当の名前……
　にこやふらめう・・・・・・・、云います」始祖村正「にこ……？」浦夢「呼びにくいでしょう。浦夢で構いません。
　私の生まれた国とこの大和は、言葉が全く
違うのです」浦夢「遠く遠く、離れていますから」始祖村正「……浦夢殿は、天竺のお人だったのか？」浦夢「いいえ。
　天竺の、更にずっと向こうです」始祖村正「西方浄土より参られたと……？」浦夢「そうですね……西の果ての国です。
　けれど、浄土ではありません」浦夢「私の生まれた国、戦争ばかりでした。
　今の大和と同じです」浦夢「だから私は、平和な楽園を求めて、旅に出ま
した」始祖村正「……」浦夢「でもそんな国、何処にもありませんでした。
　どの国も短い平和と長い争いを繰り返して
いました」浦夢「私は平和な世界を探して彷徨うより、世界
を平和にする方法を求めるべきだと、考える
ようになりました。
　そうして……あなたに出会ったのです」始祖村正「……うては一介の鍛冶師。
　しかも今は、道を見失っている」始祖村正「浦夢殿の力にはなれぬ」浦夢「いいえ。
　そんなあなたでなくてはいけません」浦夢「劒冑こそ神の子……。
　奇跡の欠片を宿す聖別の者です」浦夢「最も貴き劒冑の生誕が、人の原罪を雪そそぐ。
　神は万民を赦し、地を楽園にするでしょう」浦夢「そう……。
　正しき心を持つ鍛冶師が、真理を求めて鎚
を振るう時、苦しみの時代は終わりを告げる
に違いないのです！」始祖村正「……？
　済まぬが、わからぬ……」始祖村正「うてには……真理など……」

en: Uramu"I will teach you. Muramasa ji, please listen."Uramu"And this ideal I dream of, make it come true..."Muramasa I"............"Uramu"Long ago... in Greece, there lived a sage named Empedocles."Uramu"He explained the law of the universe. In the whole of human history, true wisdom—only this one man can be said to have it."Muramasa I"Of the universe...? Do you mean the matter you explained to me before—"Muramasa I"The three primal energies, the powers in this world: magnetic, gravitational and creative force—"Uramu"That was me developing Empedocles' ideas in my own way. Closer to physical principles, it should have come... From truth, however, it went further away."Muramasa I"...?"Uramu"He said this. The world consists of four elements and two powers..."Uramu"Earth, sun, sea and air. The power of Love joins them; the power of Strife divides them. Through that, all things manifest. So he taught."Uramu"A human being, for example, is born when Love joins the four elements in roughly equal proportions. When Strife stronger than that Love—injury or illness—attacks, the person dies."Muramasa I"Hm..."Uramu"With this theory, everything in the world can be explained. Nothing left outside."Muramasa I"Then, Uramu ji, what is justice? And evil?"Uramu"Justice and evil. You mean good and bad?"Muramasa I"Yes. That especially, please tell me."Uramu"...There are no such things."
ja:
浦夢「それをお教えします。
　村正どの、どうか聞いてください」浦夢「そして私の理想ゆめを叶えてください……」始祖村正「…………」浦夢「遠い昔……
　ぐらえきあ・・・・・に、えんぺどくれす・・・・・・・という賢者
がいました」浦夢「宇宙の理ことわりを解いた人物です。
　人間の歴史上、真の叡智の持ち主と呼べる
のは彼一人しかいません」始祖村正「宇宙の……？
　それは以前にお伺いした、あの話のことで
あろうか」始祖村正「この世には磁気、辰気、創気の三つの源気ちから
があるという――」浦夢「それは、えんぺどくれすの考えを私なりに
進めてみたものです。
　物理・・には近付いているはずですが……真理・・
からは離れてしまいました」始祖村正「……？」浦夢「彼はこう言いました。
　世界は四種の元素と二種の力で構成されて
いる……」浦夢「〝地〟〝陽〟〝海〟〝空〟の四つが〝愛〟
の力で結びつき、また〝争い〟の力で別れる
ことによって、世の万象が顕れる。
　そう説いたのです」浦夢「例えば人間は、四種類の元素がほぼ均等に
〝愛〟で結ばれることから生まれます。
　そして〝愛〟よりも強い〝争い〟の力――
怪我や病気――に襲われると死にます」始祖村正「ふむ……」浦夢「この理論で、世のあらゆる物事が説明でき
ます」始祖村正「ならば浦夢殿、正義とはいかなるものか？
　また、邪悪とは？」浦夢「正義と邪悪。
　善と悪ですか」始祖村正「うむ。
　是非とも教えて頂きたい」浦夢「……ありません」

en: Muramasa I"What?"Uramu"Such things do not exist."Muramasa I"Arre, h-how can they not exist!"Uramu"...Well. Actual substance, none. But as ways of looking at things, yes, you can say they exist."Muramasa I"Ways of looking?"
ja:
始祖村正「何？」浦夢「そんなものは、存在しないのです」始祖村正「な、無いはずはなかろう！」浦夢「……そうですね。
　実質は何もありませんが、単なる物の見方
としてなら、あるとも言えます」始祖村正「見方？」

en: Uramu"Muramasa ji. Just now, here itself, I have made one world."Uramu"Salt and water I put in a flask, stirred it, closed the lid. Inside this closed world: salt water and air. Bas, nothing else."Muramasa I"..."Uramu"Now, heat it from below with a flame—"
ja:
浦夢「村正どの。
　今、私はここに一つの世界を作りました」浦夢「ふらすこ・・・・に塩と水を入れてかき混ぜ、蓋を
しました。
　この閉じた世界には、塩水と空気しかあり
ません」始祖村正「……」浦夢「これを、下から火で熱すると」

en: Uramu"The power of Strife works. Salt and water, which were joined, separate. Water becomes vapor and mixes with air; salt returns to crystals."Muramasa I"Yes..."Uramu"Achha. In all that, where were good and evil...?"Muramasa I"..."Uramu"Put our own world in its place and think."Muramasa I"...Strife separated salt from water... Then fire is evil?"Uramu"Yes. People's connections, their bonds, these are precious. Pulling them apart, you could call that evil..."Muramasa I"So the Love that joined salt and water is justice, and the fire that pulled them apart is evil..."Uramu"But look carefully, Muramasa ji."Uramu"Salt and water separated, but water and air have newly mixed. A mist has formed."Muramasa I"...Hm?"Uramu"Between water and air, Love did its work. Matlab... that same fire was good also."Muramasa I"............"Uramu"Now, this world—shall we cool it down?"
ja:
浦夢「〝争い〟の力が働きます。
　結ばれていた塩と水が別れ、水は水蒸気と
なって空気と混ざり、塩は結晶に戻ります」始祖村正「うむ……」浦夢「さて。
　善と悪は、何処にあったでしょうか……」始祖村正「……」浦夢「我々の世界に置き換えて、考えてみてくだ
さい」始祖村正「……塩と水を引き離した〝争い〟の力……
　火が、悪なのであろうか？」浦夢「そうですね。
　人のつながり、絆は尊いものです。これを
引き離すのは罪悪だといえるでしょう……」始祖村正「塩と水を塩水にしていた〝愛〟が正義で、
引き離した火が邪悪か……」浦夢「しかし村正どの。
　よく見てください」浦夢「塩と水は別れましたが、新たに水と空気が
混ざり合い、靄もやが生まれています」始祖村正「……むぅ？」浦夢「水と空気の間に〝愛〟が働いたのです。
　ということは……火は善でもあったのです」始祖村正「…………」浦夢「今度はこの世界を冷やしてみましょうか」

en: Uramu"Cool the mist... and the water falls as drops."Uramu"The drops dissolve the salt, becoming salt water again."Muramasa I"..."Uramu"Salt water it produced, so cooling was a good act. But the mist it broke apart. Evil also, same cooling."Muramasa I"Ngh... Hmm..."Uramu"Do you understand, Muramasa ji?"Uramu"Good and evil—"Muramasa I"...One thing, front and back only?"Uramu"Yes. One act, you stand on a particular side and call it good. Go to the opposite side, now you call it evil."Uramu"Bas. This much only."Muramasa I"............"Uramu"But this good and evil, people make such a tremendously important matter of it. Without knowing—or knowing very well."Muramasa I"Why...?"Uramu"The Love that benefits them, they want to approve. The Strife that costs them, that they want to reject."Muramasa I"..."Uramu"This self-righteousness is the devil's curse binding human hearts."Uramu"Muramasa ji... now you understand, no? Why is peace not staying? Why does war come back, again and again?"Uramu"Because—water wants love for water only! Air wants it for air only! Salt, salt only!"Muramasa I"————"
ja:
浦夢「靄を冷やすと……
　水は水滴となって落ちます」浦夢「水滴は塩を溶かし、再び塩水になります」始祖村正「……」浦夢「塩水を生んだのですから、冷やしたのは善
の行いですね。
　しかし靄を分解してしまったので、悪でも
あります」始祖村正「ぬ……むぅ」浦夢「村正どの。わかりましたか」浦夢「善と悪は――」始祖村正「……裏表・・でしかない、と？」浦夢「そうです。
　ある行いを、特定の視点から見た時に善と
呼び、逆方向から見た時は悪と呼ぶ」浦夢「それだけのことに過ぎないのです」始祖村正「…………」浦夢「しかし人々は、この善悪をさも重大なもの
であるかのように扱っています。
　無意識に――あるいは意識的に」始祖村正「何故……？」浦夢「自分の利益になる〝愛〟を肯定し、自分の
損失になる〝争い〟を否定するためです」始祖村正「……」浦夢「この独善こそ、人の心を縛る悪魔の呪い」浦夢「村正どの……もうおわかりでしょう。
　どうして平和は永く続かないのか？
　どうして戦争は繰り返されるのか？」浦夢「それは――
　水は水だけの愛を、空気は空気だけの愛を、
塩は塩だけの愛を求めるからです！」始祖村正「――――」

en: Uramu"Muramasa ji..."Muramasa I"Then—"Muramasa I"To put the world right—"Uramu"Destroy self-righteousness!"Uramu"Let people know the truth Empedocles discovered."Uramu"Break their curse! Trapped in love for themselves only, they keep fighting—free them from that curse!"Uramu"This kind of miracle, only a tsurugi can do. God's tsurugi—you must make it!"Muramasa I"............ Will it be possible...?"Muramasa I"This Muramasa... such a great work, can I do it...?"Uramu"You can!"Uramu"Skill you have. Knowledge I have given you."Uramu"And the power is here—"
ja:
浦夢「村正どの……」始祖村正「ならば」始祖村正「世界を正すには」浦夢「〝独善〟を滅ぼすのです！」浦夢「えんぺどくれすの見つけた真理を、人々に
知らしめてください」浦夢「彼らを呪いから解き放つのです！
　自分だけの愛に囚われて争い合う呪いから」浦夢「そんな奇跡を成し得るものは……劒冑しか
ありません。
　あなたが、神の劒冑を造るのです！」始祖村正「…………。
　できようか……？」始祖村正「この村正に……そこまでの大業が……」浦夢「できます！」浦夢「あなたには技があります。
　知識は、私が教えました」浦夢「そして力は、ここに――」

en: Muramasa I"What is this? Crystal... No, not that...!?"Muramasa I"...I-I cannot identify it! An Emishi, and a mineral I don't know?! How is this possible!!"Uramu"Of course you don't know it. On this whole earth, probably this is the only one..."Uramu"Lapis Sagii—a fragment of the sacred body. God's flesh and blood."Muramasa I"...God...!? No—this I can feel! Something tremendous... definitely, this is!!"Uramu"Yes. This stone has power enough to make a person immortal."Uramu"Like this..."
ja:
始祖村正「これは？
　水晶すいそう……いや違う……!?」始祖村正「……わ、わからぬ！
　馬鹿なっ、蝦夷の知らぬ鉱物など!!」浦夢「知らないのは当然です。
　これはおそらく、地上に一つきりしかない
もの……」浦夢「聖骸断片らぴす・さぎー。
　神の血肉です」始祖村正「……神……!?
　いや、わかる！　確かにこれは――途方も
なきものだ!!」浦夢「はい。
　この石は人を不死にするほどの力を持って
います」浦夢「このように……」

en: Muramasa I"U-Uramu ji... Your body!?"Uramu"..."Muramasa I"The same as... this stone?"Uramu"Yes. Since I obtained this stone, no aging... and little by little, my body went on changing into this."Uramu"Before the whole body changed, I could meet you... I could tell you everything. Achha hua. That much went right."Uramu"The mission God gave me... it seems I have completed it."
ja:
始祖村正「う、浦夢殿……
　その体は!?」浦夢「……」始祖村正「この石と……同じ？」浦夢「ええ。
　この石を手に入れてから、私は歳を取らず
……そして体は次第に、このように変わって
いきました」浦夢「全身が変わる前に、あなたに会えて……
　全てを伝えることができて、良かった」浦夢「私は……
　神より授かった使命を、果たせたようです」

en: Muramasa I"Uramu ji!"Uramu"...So long... Too much I have lived..."Uramu"Now at last... I can sleep..."Muramasa I"No! This—is it this stone—"Uramu"No. That is for you. You must use it."Uramu"To make the supreme tsurugi."Muramasa I"B-but—"Uramu"Please. I entrust... everything to you."Uramu"Free people from self-righteousness."Uramu"Not one person's love, but everybody's love... Guide them toward universal love! All things joined, no distinctions made, no conflict raised!"Uramu"God's—love...! Into this world... please, bring it!!"
ja:
始祖村正「浦夢殿！」浦夢「……長く……
　あまりにも長く、生きました……」浦夢「ようやく眠れます……」始祖村正「いかぬ！
　これか――この石を」浦夢「いけません。
　それはあなたが使うのです」浦夢「至高の劒冑を造るために」始祖村正「し、しかし」浦夢「お願いします。
　あなたに全て……託します」浦夢「人を独善から解き放つのです」浦夢「一人の愛ではなく、全員の愛を……
　争いを起こさず、万物を分け隔てなく結び
つける、普遍の愛を求める道へ――いざなう
のです！」浦夢「神の――愛を……！
　この世界に、どうか!!」

en: Muramasa I"U-Uramu ji..."Muramasa I"Uramu JIII!!"
ja: 始祖村正「う、浦夢殿……」始祖村正「浦夢殿ぉぉぉっっ!!」

en: Muramasa I"Listen well. My daughter. My granddaughter."Muramasa I"Now hear the law, the way our Muramasa forging will follow."Muramasa II"Yes."Muramasa"Yes."Muramasa I"A tsurugi is an instrument of arms. A thing made for war."Muramasa I"So first we must look at war properly. This thing called war—what is it?"Muramasa II"..."Muramasa I"Not the work of goodness! Not justice showing its face!"Muramasa I"My love, my desire, must be satisfied, so I destroy his love. That is war. Martial force is the violence that does it."Muramasa I"Self-righteousness! THIS is evil!!"Muramasa"————"Muramasa II"...Then?"Muramasa I"We Muramasa will finish war itself. Let people know its evil, and drive it out of the human world!"Muramasa I"Not just give violence one more helping hand. We will forge tsurugi to hold that hand down!!"Muramasa II"So this is the answer you have reached, Baba."Muramasa I"It is."Muramasa II"Then my trust is in it! The path you have set, I will follow. Your work I will carry on."Muramasa II"After me, this one carries it on!"Muramasa"Y-yes!"Muramasa II"Baba, now leave the worrying and start forging."Muramasa I"Haan. But not me alone. You also must forge."Muramasa II"Hm? Two tsurugi to present, you mean?"Muramasa I"Yes. But not both to one side. Southern Court gets one. Northern Court gets one."Muramasa I"Both sides' violence must be restrained together. Otherwise this fighting will not finish."Muramasa II"That makes sense."Muramasa I"No objection, then?"Muramasa II"Of course not! To become the tsurugi that gives your ideal its body—this was my wish all along."Muramasa II"And here, no worry left behind. Every technique I have already taught this one."Muramasa"..."Muramasa II"Tomorrow we begin forging."Muramasa II"Now I know what you want: use a tsurugi to break the blade inside people's hearts. That wish, Baba, I will fulfil!"Muramasa I"Yes...!"
ja:
始祖村正「聞けい。
　我が娘よ。我が孫よ」始祖村正「これより村正鍛冶の法みちを告げる」二世村正「うむ」村正「はい」始祖村正「劒冑とは武の器。
　戦のためのもの」始祖村正「ゆえにまず、戦を鑑みる。
　戦とは如何なるものなのか――」二世村正「……」始祖村正「善の働きに非ず！
　正義の顕れに非ず！」始祖村正「戦とは我ワレの愛のぞみを求めて彼カレの愛を壊す行為おこない。
　武とはその暴力」始祖村正「独善なり！
　これこそが悪!!」村正「――――」二世村正「……では？」始祖村正「我ら村正は戦を滅ぼす。
　戦の悪を人々に知らしめ、戦を人の世から
去らしめる！」始祖村正「武にただ加担するのではなく、
　武を制するための劒冑を打つ!!」二世村正「それが御父の行き着いた答なのだな」始祖村正「そうだ」二世村正「ならば、信ずる！
　吾あれは御父の定めた道に従い、後を継ごうぞ」二世村正「吾の後は、こやつが継ぐ！」村正「は……はい！」二世村正「御父は心置きなく、鍛造に掛かるが良い」始祖村正「うむ。
　だが、うてだけではない。なれも鍛えよ」二世村正「む、それは？
　劒冑を二領、献上するということか？」始祖村正「そうだ。但し一方にではない。
　南朝と北朝に、一領ずつ」始祖村正「両陣の武を共に抑えねば、乱は治められぬ」二世村正「道理だ」始祖村正「否やはあるまいな？」二世村正「無論！
　御父の理想を体現する劒冑と成ることこそ、
吾が宿望であった」二世村正「後顧の憂いもない。
　こやつには既に、全ての技を伝えてある」村正「……」二世村正「明日より早速、鍛造に掛かろうぞ」二世村正「御父の望みが、劒冑をもって人の心中の刃
を砕くにあると知ったからには……
　その望み、必ずや吾が果たす！」始祖村正「うむ……！」

en:
The years had been shooting past me like arrows. Here, all at once, their sharpness went.

My Muramasa—the third generation—probably had not seen most of what followed herself. A few short images, information apparently heard from others: all bundled together and sliding through my awareness.
ja:
矢の如く俺・の前を過ぎていった光陰は――
　ここから急に、精彩を失う。

　三世おれの村正は、これ以降の事変の殆どを自分の眼では
見なかったのだろう。
　幾つかの短い映像と伝聞で得たらしき情報とがひと
まとめに、俺の認識上を滑ってゆく。

en:
Founder Muramasa and Second Muramasa were finally complete. Performance-wise, naturally they stood at the very top. But two extraordinary properties came with them. These belonged to the Sengo Muramasa line alone.

First: the Balance of Good and Evil.

Kill one enemy, kill one ally also. Kill one evil person, kill one good person also. Kill someone you hate, and someone you love must die by your hand.

Bond with Muramasa and this law becomes your burden.

My good is good. His good is evil. Therefore he must be removed. This self-righteous arrangement, Muramasa would not let her warrior force through by violence.

Use her overwhelming might to get what you want, and your own hands end up smashing that very wish. Strongest warrior of all, and yet nobody could afford less freedom with his strength. That was the man he would have to become.

Second: Mental Synchronisation.

Muramasa could release Waves, laying her pilot's mind over the minds of people nearby. The Balance of Good and Evil, already soaked into that pilot's mind, would be copied across also. One entire army could become a group following Muramasa's doctrine.

A warrior's armour plating could protect him against the Waves. For that obstacle also, a variation existed: Eggs. Even his mind could not escape.

Plant an Egg inside a tsurugi. It grows, hatches, and turns the tsurugi into a relay point for the Waves. The new Waves reach the nearest person first. Meaning, the pilot sitting inside that very tsurugi.

Now, let a Muramasa pilot have any selfishness in him. Will he volunteer his own army for Mental Synchronisation? Hardly. Use it on the enemy, take away their will to fight.

For this exact reason, the founder prepared two tsurugi and gave one to each side. Each Muramasa warrior uses Mental Synchronisation on the enemy. Neither side alone gets the upper hand.

Across the whole battlefield, the Balance of Good and Evil would rule.

Perfect. You could call it that. The founder's ideal had taken shape in his tsurugi; further improvement, where was the room?

These tsurugi would surely bring peace. The long conflict between the Northern and Southern Courts would come to a peaceful end.

Founder Muramasa believed it.
His daughter, Second Muramasa, believed it. His granddaughter, Third Muramasa, had no doubts either.
ja:
遂に完成した始祖村正そして二世村正、この二領の
劒冑は性能において頂点へ達していたのは無論だが、
加えて異常な特質を備えてもいた。
　それは千子村正だけのものであり、二つあった。

　一つは〝善悪相殺〟の戒律である。
　対敵を一人殺したなら味方も一人。悪しき者を一人
殺したなら善き者も一人。憎む者を一人殺したなら、
愛する者もまた一人、殺さねばならない。

　村正と結縁した武者はこの掟を背負う。
　己の善のみ盲信し、敵の善は悪と看做して排除する、
その〝独善〟を力で押し通すことを、村正という劒冑
は許さないのだ。

　衆に卓抜する村正の暴威ちからで望みを遂げようとすれば、
己の手でその望みを打ち砕く結末に至る。
　村正武者は最強にして、誰よりも武力の行使を自重
する人物にならざるを得ないであろう。

　もう一つは〝精神同調〟の能わざである。
　村正は『波』を放散し、周囲の人間の精神に仕手の
それを重ねることができるのだ。

　仕手の精神に浸透した善悪相殺の戒律も写される。
　一軍全体を、村正の思想に沿う集団へと変貌せしめ
られるのである。

　武者ならば甲鉄の防護力をもって『波』の力に抵抗
するも可能だが……
　村正はこの能力の変形として『卵』を生成する事で、
遂には武者の精神をも逃さぬのだった。

『卵』は劒冑に移植されると内部で生育、やがて孵化
し、劒冑を『波』の中継点・・・に造り替える。
　新たに発散される『波』の影響を第一に受けるのは、
最も近くにいる者、つまりその劒冑の仕手である……。

　村正の仕手に利己心あらば、この〝精神同調〟能力
を味方の軍に対して使おうとは思わないであろう。
　敵軍に対して用い、戦意を奪おうとする筈である。

　しかし、だからこそ始祖村正は劒冑を二領用意して、
対立する両陣営に与えたのだ。
　双方の村正武者が敵に対して〝精神同調〟を行使し
合えば、一方だけが優勢になるような事態は起きない。

　戦場は遍あまねく〝善悪相殺〟の戒律に支配される。

　完璧――そう言って良かった。
　始祖村正が劒冑に懸けた理想は、これ以上はないと
いう形で結実した。

　この劒冑は必ずや世に平和をもたらす。
　長きに渡り続いた南北朝の乱を、穏健に終息させる。

　始祖村正はそう信じた。
　二世村正むすめも信じ、三世村正まごも疑わなかった。

en:
............Except.

I lived in a later age. I knew the facts had not gone according to this excellent arrangement.

Shanti aa jayegi. Peace will come. Such a complete plan, with an answer ready for every objection. Unfortunately, the world had not attended the explanation.

The age of the Northern and Southern Courts ended with a war of annihilation without precedent. In just one year, some accounts say a tenth of the entire population died. Others say more than a fifth.

The Armour of Calamity.
History would remember the name Sengo Uemon-no-jou Muramasa: a line of demon armour that ended in its third generation.
ja:
…………が。

　事実はそうならなかったことを、後世に生きる俺は
知っている。

　南北朝の時代は――
　その最後に未曾有の殲滅戦争を巻き起こし、わずか
一年で当時の全人口の一割とも二割以上とも云われる
死者を出して、閉幕へ至るのだ。

　災厄の劒冑。
　三代で絶えた妖甲の一門、千子右衛門尉村正の銘なを
歴史に刻んで。

en:
An elegant place, but quiet about it. Some palace's inner garden, perhaps. That was the feeling.

There I—Muramasa—lay prostrate. Someone was standing on the steps ahead, apparently looking down at me.

No one else here. People could be sensed nearby, but it seemed they had been made to stay away.
ja:
そこは雅やかで、されど落ち着いた佇まいだった。
　何処かの御殿の、内庭……そんな風情だ。

　その場で、俺――村正は平伏している。
　前方の段階きざはしには誰かが立ち、こちらを見下ろしてい
る様子であった。

　人は、それきり。
　辺りに気配はあるが、遠ざけられているようだ。

en: Southern Emperor"You are Muramasa's granddaughter... the third generation?"Muramasa"Y-yes. Y-Your Majesty—"Southern Emperor"Enough. No public here, no council of state. This language you are not used to, leave it aside."Muramasa"Y-yes..."
ja:
南朝帝「そなたが村正の孫……三代目か」村正「は……っ、はい。
　へ、陛下に置かれましては――」南朝帝「良い。今は公衆の前でも朝議の場でもない。
　慣れぬ言葉遣いは無用にいたせ」村正「は、はい……」

en:
...Your Majesty.
So the Emperor, this was. Probably the Southern Court's.
ja:
……陛下。
　では、この御方は帝か。おそらく南朝の。

en: Southern Emperor"You will already have heard..."Muramasa"..."Southern Emperor"Muramasa, your house will end. No succession, in any form, is permitted."Southern Emperor"Let the line of the tsurugi smith Uemon-no-jou Muramasa end with you."Muramasa"............ I understand."Muramasa"My family's crimes... the calamity we brought... Considering that, even if all our kin, back through our ancestors, were put to the sword, what right would I have to complain?"Muramasa"Your Majesty's mercy... for that, I am grateful..."Southern Emperor"...Yes..."
ja:
南朝帝「既に聞いておろうが……」村正「……」南朝帝「村正、そなたの家門は――これを断絶する。
　一切の継承は許さぬ」南朝帝「劒冑鍛冶右衛門尉村正は、そなたをもって
終えよ」村正「…………。
　承知して、おります」村正「我が一門の犯したる罪……招きたる災いの
程を思えば……
　祖先に遡り、一族係累鏖殺の憂目に遭おう
とも恨み言は申せませぬところ」村正「陛下の御慈悲に……感謝いたします……」南朝帝「……うむ……」

en:
The ending of a house.

For a medieval person, how much weight was in those words? A modern man like me had no way of knowing.

Muramasa's trembling hands... the drops falling onto the white sand. From these only, I could try to understand.

All for their crimes. For the calamity they had brought.◆

Calamity.
What that calamity actually was, her mind showed it. Into mine also it came.

I learned the truth hidden in the final tragedy of the Northern and Southern Courts.
ja:
家門断絶。
　中世の価値観においてその一事がどれほどの重みを
持つのか。現代人には知る由もないことだ。

　ただ、村正の両手の震えと……
　白砂の上へしたたり落ちる雫から、推し量るしかな
かった。

　全ては罪のため。招いた災いのため。◆

　災い・・。
　村正の心にその実相が映り、俺の心にも写る。

　俺は知った。
　南北朝時代最後の惨劇――そこに秘められた真実を。

en:
————One accident. Everything went wrong from there.

When the Northern commander received Founder Muramasa, his hold on power was hardly firm. A ruler, less; a man keeping his generals' competing interests from pulling the army apart, more.

With his politically gifted younger brother's help, he was only just managing to hold it together. Let circumstances shift a little, let someone's interests change, and hostility was ready. Yesterday's subordinate standing up against him was no rare thing.

Not long after he obtained Muramasa, it happened. In the bustle before a campaign, an assassin slipped close to him and attacked without warning.

Battle-hardened, the commander drew his sword by reflex and cut the assassin—
Killed him.

Muramasa's law allowed no exception. One enemy killed, and against his own will the blade turned back. It cut down the ally beside him.

His beloved younger brother. The man supporting him in public life and private life both.

...From that day, the Northern army became a body of madness. The commander lost his reason and scattered Mental Synchronisation's Waves without distinction. His own madness spread through the entire force.

Mad general, mad soldiers: facing them, the Southern commander with Second Muramasa had only one way to protect his people from those Waves. Put his whole army under his own mental influence first.

And so a struggle without precedent began. Hell, here on earth.

One side was a pack of beasts, destroying and killing anything that came before it. The other was an army of anguish: kill an enemy soldier, then kill one friend fighting shoulder to shoulder with you.

The end of the world, visible before the eyes. Human lives were cut down like rice in an autumn field, without a second thought, and sent across the river of the dead.

How many people died, how many villages vanished... Exact numbers, nobody knew. Probably nobody had the will to know either.

While it went on, surviving was all people could struggle for. After it ended, the ruined world left them only staring.

The Southern commander and his thirteen warriors challenged the Northern commander and Founder Muramasa, with their godlike power. At last they defeated them and cut off the source of the turmoil. By then, it was said:

〝In Yamato now, the dogs and cats that feed on corpses prosper more than people.〟

A monk's lament.
ja:
――――たった一つの事故が何もかも狂わせた。

　始祖村正を贈られた北朝軍の主将は、当時、堅牢な
権力基盤を有しているとは言い難い状況にあった。
　支配者というよりも、諸将の利害調整役という立場
に近かった。

　政治の才に優れた実弟の力を借りて、漸ようよう軍をまと
めていたのである。
　些細な情勢の変化、利害関係の変動から敵意を買い、
昨日までの部下に盾突かれることも一切ではなかった。

　それは彼が村正を手に入れてまだ程ない頃のことで
ある。
　出陣前の慌しさに紛れて刺客が主将の側まで近付き、
不意に襲い掛かった。

　戦慣れした主将は反射的に抜刀し、刺客を斬り――
　殺してしまったのだ。

　村正の戒律が持つ拘束力は絶対である。
　敵を殺した彼は自分の意思によらずして刃の向きを
返し、傍らに立つ味方を斬り伏せた。

　公私両面で彼を支えてくれていた、最愛の弟を。

　……その日から、北朝軍は狂気の集団と化した。
　発狂した主将が〝精神同調〟の波を無差別に放散し、
全軍に己おのが狂気を蔓延させたのである。

　狂将率いる狂兵の群れを迎えて――
　二世村正を持つ南朝方の主将は、狂気の『波』から
味方を守るため、先んじて全軍を自分の精神影響下へ
置くよりほかに手立てがなくなった。

　かくして前例のない地獄的な闘争が地上に発現する。

　一方は、手当たり次第何もかも破壊し殺し尽くさん
とする魔獣の群れ。
　一方は、敵兵を一人殺す都度、肩並べて戦う友をも
一人ずつ殺してゆく悲愴の軍団。

　末世の相そのものであった。
　この世において人間の生命は秋の田の稲穂のように、
無造作に刈り取られ、三途の川の向こうへ流された。

　どれほどの人が死に、どれほどの村が滅んだか……
　正確に知る者など誰もいない。知ろうとする意欲を
持つ者もいなかったろう。

　乱の最中、人々はただ生き延びるために必死であり、
乱が果てた後は、世間の惨状にただ呆然とするばかり
であった。

　神懸かりの力を揮ふるった始祖村正と北朝主将に南朝の
将とその麾下十三騎が挑み、遂にこれを討ち果たして
乱の源を断った時――曰く「いまや大和では人よりも、
死肉を食らう犬猫の方が栄えている」……。

　ある法師の嘆弁である。

en: Southern Emperor"Muramasa..."Muramasa"..."Southern Emperor"I know well that your family bore no evil intention. You wished to end the age of war..."Southern Emperor"At the root, it is my own guilt that weighs heavy. I went on with the war, paying no heed to the people's suffering. A little sooner, had I made peace with the Northern Court, this would not have happened."Muramasa"............"Southern Emperor"Heaven will punish my crime in due course."Southern Emperor"But... even so, Muramasa. This state has been entrusted to me. Those who brought disaster on it, I cannot pardon. Your grandfather and mother especially..."Southern Emperor"The founder Muramasa was shattered. Nothing of him remains. Kusunoki's second Muramasa is gravely damaged... but has not perished..."Southern Emperor"It... cannot be left as it is."Muramasa"...!"Southern Emperor"It will be broken and melted down soon. Understand this."Muramasa"...W-wait... Your Majesty!"Southern Emperor"..."Muramasa"Please... bas, not that!"Southern Emperor"You ask me not to destroy the second Muramasa?"Muramasa"For an Emishi, becoming a tsurugi is the deepest wish. To fall in battle and decay into the earth, that also is fulfilment."Muramasa"B-but... After becoming a tsurugi, to be turned back into scrap and thrown away without a battle—for an Emishi, for a smith, that suffering is worse than death, worse than hell!"Southern Emperor"...I see. Yes... that is so..."Southern Emperor"But a death in battle means somebody must wear that terrible tsurugi again. Tell me, can I permit such a thing?"Muramasa"............"
ja:
南朝帝「村正よ……」村正「……」南朝帝「そなたら一門に悪心がなかったことは良く
わかっている。
　乱世を収めたかったのであろう……」南朝帝「元を糺せば、民の苦難も顧みず戦を続けた
朕の罪こそ重い……。
　もそっと早く、北朝と和しておれば、この
ような仕儀とはならなんだ」村正「…………」南朝帝「いずれ朕の罪は天の罰するところとなろう」南朝帝「が……それでも村正よ、朕は社稷しゃしょくを預かる
者として、国土に災禍をもたらしたそなたら
を許すわけにはゆかぬ。
　わけてもそなたの祖父と母は……」南朝帝「始祖村正は粉々に砕かれ、既に跡形もない。
　楠木の二世村正は深く傷ついたが……まだ
滅びておらぬ……」南朝帝「これを……このままにはしておけぬ」村正「……！」南朝帝「近いうちに砕き、鋳潰す……。
　さよう心得よ」村正「……お、お待ちを……
　陛下！」南朝帝「……」村正「どうか……その儀ばかりは！」南朝帝「二世村正を潰すなと云うか」村正「蝦夷にとり、劒冑となるは本望。
　戦場いくさばにて斃され、土に朽ちるもまた本望」村正「さ、されど……
　ひとたび劒冑となりながら、戦なき場所で
鉄屑に戻され棄てられるは――蝦夷として、
鍛冶師として、死にも堕獄にも勝る痛哭！」南朝帝「……そうか。
　そうであったのう……」南朝帝「だが戦で葬るには、今一度、あの恐ろしき
劒冑を誰かに装甲さまとわせねばならぬ……。
　さようなことを、朕が許せると思うてか」村正「…………」

en: Muramasa"A vessel of war ought to decay on a battlefield... If that cannot be, it would rather be sealed away, sleep forever, and be forgotten."Muramasa"Please, Your Majesty...! I offer this head with my plea."Southern Emperor"..."Muramasa"Just now, Your Majesty yourself acknowledged it. My grandfather and mother had no malice. They wanted only to end the age of war."Muramasa"That is how it was! Whatever my forebears got wrong, that one wish... that at least must have been right...!"Muramasa"If Second Muramasa, my mother, is given the lowest end a tsurugi can suffer... that ideal, that wish also will be defiled!"Southern Emperor"............"Muramasa"You may bury her in the earth. Sink her into the sea."Muramasa"But please... don't melt her down..."Southern Emperor"..."Southern Emperor"Bury it, someone may dig it up. Sink it, someone may pull it out again."Southern Emperor"Then Muramasa's tsurugi may return to Yamato... and turn the earth to hell once more."Muramasa"...Ngh."Southern Emperor"Muramasa. Your head, you offered. Those were not empty words?"Muramasa"N-no falsehood!"Muramasa"Whenever you wish, if you will grant mercy."Southern Emperor"Very well. Third Muramasa, I command you—"Southern Emperor"Forge a tsurugi."Muramasa"...!?"
ja:
村正「武の器は戦場にて朽ちねばならぬもの……
　それが叶わぬならいっそ封印され、永劫の
眠りにつき、忘れ去られるを望むものにござ
います」村正「どうか、陛下……！
　この首を献じて、お願い申し上げます」南朝帝「……」村正「先ほど、陛下はお認め下さいました……。
　祖父と母に悪心は無かったと。乱世に幕を
引きたかっただけなのだと」村正「その通りなのです！
　我が祖おやが、何を誤っていたとしても、その
願いだけは……正しかった筈なのです……！」村正「二世ははが劒冑として最も卑しき最期を遂げれ
ば……その理念ねがいまでも汚されてしまいます！」南朝帝「…………」村正「土に埋めて頂いても構いません。
　海に沈めて頂いても構いません」村正「ですがどうか、鋳潰しだけはお許しを……」南朝帝「……」南朝帝「土に埋めても、掘り返されるやもしれぬ。
　海に沈めても、引き上げられるやもしれぬ」南朝帝「そうして、村正の劒冑が大和に還り……
　再び、地上を地獄に変えるやもしれぬ」村正「……っ」南朝帝「村正よ。
　首を献ずるとの言葉に、嘘はあるまいな」村正「は――はい！」村正「御寛恕を賜れるのであれば、いつなりと」南朝帝「宜しい。
　ならば三世村正、そなたに命ずる」南朝帝「劒冑を打て」村正「……!?」

en: Southern Emperor"Become a tsurugi equal to your mother."Southern Emperor"Then sleep beside her in some mountain's shadow. Forever, if we may hope for it."Southern Emperor"But... there is a reason I am sealing you together. That you understand, surely."Muramasa"..."Southern Emperor"If someday someone breaks the seal and takes Second Muramasa, you also must find a pilot, a master."Southern Emperor"Then keep watch on your mother. If she is used to bring peace, as your grandfather wished, well and good. But if once again she becomes a warrior of calamity, as she did in this age—"Southern Emperor"You must destroy the second Muramasa."Muramasa"............"Southern Emperor"If you say you cannot, then she must after all be melted down."Southern Emperor"Answer, third generation. Can you destroy your mother...?"Muramasa"I-I can! Your command, I will carry it out without fail!"Southern Emperor"Good."Southern Emperor"Then hear it again. Once you become a tsurugi, only when your mother is released may you bond with a warrior."Southern Emperor"Until then, the sword-bearing ceremony is forbidden with anyone. No one."Muramasa"Yes."Southern Emperor"One more thing. Forged by your grandfather's secret method, you too will possess that abominable ability, will you not?"Southern Emperor"Those Waves that invade human hearts, you too will command them, yes?"
