ja:
家屋の陰から若い男が一人、顔を覗かせた。
　俺を見た後、記憶を探るように一度首を傾げ、再び
こちらへ目をやる。

en: Refugee B"You're yesterday's drunkard, no?"Kageaki"..."Muramasa"...Yesterday night seems to have been quite an entertainment for you."
ja:
難民Ｂ「ゆうべの酔っ払いじゃないか」景明「…………」村正「……貴方、昨日の夜は随分と面白いことに
なってたみたいね」

en:
The same greeting as before. Exactly the same. From behind, a look and a few words were entering me with considerable sharpness. I maintained the face of a man to whom no information had reached.

At least he recognised me. That much could be put to use.
ja:
先刻と全く同じ声の掛けられ方に、背後からやけに
痛い視線と言葉が突き刺さっていたが、気付かぬ風を
取り繕っておく。
　ともあれ、これは奇貨だった。

en: Kageaki"For the disturbance I caused, my apologies."Refugee B"No... let it be. I think you helped us out, actually."Refugee B"But here, what brings you?"Kageaki"There is something I would like to ask—"
ja:
景明「その節はお騒がせしました」難民Ｂ「いや……いいよ。
　あんたのお陰で助かった気もするしさ」難民Ｂ「それで、なんでこんな所に来たんだ？」景明「少々、お伺いしたい事があり――」

en:
I stopped halfway and hesitated. In what capacity was I asking? That would have to be stated. But would identifying myself as police improve matters with this man?

A welcome with open arms was probably not coming. On the other hand, without mentioning the police, my official designation remained Yesterday's Drunkard. Under that designation I could hardly expect a serious hearing.

...Kya karein. The introduction would have to be made.
ja:
言いかけて、逡巡する。
　話を聞くには聞くなりの立場を示さねばならないが
……彼に対して警官という名乗りは有効だろうか？

　おそらく単純に好意では迎えられまい。
　とはいえ、警察を自称しないのであれば俺の立場は
昨日の酔漢のままである。まともに相手をして貰える
とは思えなかった。

　……止む無し。

en: Kageaki"Excuse me. I am from the police."Refugee B"...POLICE?!"
ja: 景明「失礼、自分は警察に属している者です」難民Ｂ「……警察!?」

en:
Yes. Precisely the welcome anticipated. The young man's face visibly tightened; all around us, the quiet presences began to stir.

By law, these people could not be counted as regular citizens of Kamakura. For them, the police were not protectors. Quite possibly the opposite. I quickly tried to remove that fear, before my introduction did any more work on its own.
ja:
案の定だった。
　若い男の表情が露骨に引き攣り、周囲の押し殺した
気配もざわり・・・と波立つ。

　法制上、正規の鎌倉市民とは言えない彼らにとって、
警察は保護者ではないのだ。
　むしろ逆だろう――その点の危惧を拭うため、俺は
すぐ言葉を継いだ。

en: Kageaki"Please don't worry. Asking you to vacate is not what I have come for."Refugee B"..."Kageaki"I am here to find out how things stand with you. If you are willing, I would like to hear it from you."Refugee B"...Hear it, and then do what?"Kageaki"Until I know the details, I cannot say."Refugee B"In the end you will start driving us out only, no?"Kageaki"I cannot rule that out."
ja:
景明「御安心下さい。
　立ち退きの勧告に来たのではありません」難民Ｂ「……」景明「貴方がたの状況を調査するために参ったの
です。
　宜しければ、お話を伺いたいのですが」難民Ｂ「……聞いてどうする？」景明「詳しい事を知るまでは、何とも」難民Ｂ「結局は追い出しに掛かるんじゃないか？」景明「否定はできません」

en:
Clever promises I could give. The resulting pain in my own chest would also be mine to enjoy. I answered him honestly.

The army or police might very well try to settle the refugee problem with exactly that sort of shortsighted measure.
ja:
巧言を弄んでも自分の胸が苦しくなるだけだ。
　俺は正直なところを答えた。

　実際、軍あるいは警察がそうした短絡的措置で難民
問題の解決を図る事は充分に有り得る。

en: Refugee B"..."Kageaki"...But I think it would be better if that did not happen. Of my own capacity I have no grand opinion. Even so... perhaps something can be done from my side."Kageaki"Will you help me in this?"Refugee B"...Well. Talking, at least, we can do."Refugee B"Our life is already like this. Talking will make it worse also, or what..."Kageaki"Thank you."
ja:
難民Ｂ「……」景明「……しかし、自分はそうならぬ方が良いと
考えています。
　自分の力量は高が知れていますが……それ
でも何かできる事はあるかもしれません」景明「御協力を頂けないでしょうか」難民Ｂ「…………。
　まぁ、話くらいなら」難民Ｂ「別にそれで俺達の生活がこれ以上悪くなる
わけじゃないしな……」景明「有難うございます」

en: Reluctant agreement. I bowed nonetheless.
ja: 消極的な同意だったが、ともかく俺は頭を下げた。

en: Kageaki"Where have you all come from?"Refugee B"Different places. I am from Suruga. Others came from Totomi, Owari..."Refugee B"Mostly the Tokai region, though. Some came from farther away, but not many."Kageaki"...I see."
ja:
景明「貴方がたは、どちらから？」難民Ｂ「そりゃ、色々だよ。
　俺は駿河だけど、他にも遠江とか尾張とか」難民Ｂ「でも大半は東海地方だな。
　もっと遠くから来た奴もいることはいるが、
多くはない」景明「……成程」

en:
So these were people driven out by the struggle between Raichou Imagawa and Yukitsura Ashikaga in Kinki and Tokai. The fight for control of Rokuhara had been fierce. These people's homes had gone in it; they had escaped as far as Kamakura.

Go back, go somewhere else—probably neither option was left to them now.
ja:
つまりこの難民キャンプは、近畿東海で展開される
今川雷蝶と足利幸行ゆきつらの抗争に逐われた人々の集まりか。
　六波羅の主権を競う激闘で住処を奪われ、鎌倉まで
逃げ延びてきたというわけだ。

　彼らにはもはや帰る所も行く所も無いだろう。

en: Kageaki"For the time being, you want to live in Kamakura, then."Refugee B"What other option is there...?"Kageaki"Is there anything you are finding difficult?"Refugee B"Difficult? Only houses, food and jobs are short. That much only."
ja:
景明「当面、鎌倉で暮らす事を御希望なのですね」難民Ｂ「他にどうしようもないからな……」景明「何か不自由されている事は？」難民Ｂ「不自由？
　家と、食い物と、働き口が足りないくらい
だよ」

en:
He answered with a shrug. A question whose answer required no asking, and I had asked it.

The same troubles were spreading among the regular citizens. Here they existed in a more severe form. For solving that, my capabilities were not sufficient. We could only hope for the authorities to act in the future.

Something smaller, perhaps. That was the scale on which I could be of use.
ja:
肩をすくめて、答える男。
　訊く必要も無くもがなの事ではあった。

　要するに、正規の市民の間でも広がっている問題が
彼らにはより深刻な問題として存在するという事だ。
　……この解決は俺の能力の及ぶところではなかった。
将来的な行政に期待するほかない。

　俺にできるのは、もっと小さな事だろう。

en: Kageaki"I have also heard there is trouble between you and the established residents."Refugee B"Haan... we are not welcome. So this trouble, that trouble, something keeps happening."Refugee B"Honestly, their side I understand. A whole crowd in dirty clothes suddenly pours into your town. Who will feel happy about that?"Kageaki"..."Refugee B"But we came here because there was nowhere else. They say get out. Achha, get out and go where? We cannot just nod and leave."Kageaki"Yes."Refugee B"Somehow... I wish they would accept us."Kageaki"I understand there was an incident that made relations much worse."Refugee B"The bridge, you mean?"Kageaki"Yes."Refugee B"They say we broke it. We would never do that..."Refugee B"Who here has that much energy left, you tell me?"Kageaki"..."Refugee B"And benefit? What benefit comes to us? Nothing. It is complete bakwaas."Kageaki"Then who do you think did it?"Refugee B"Who knows? Some troublemaker having his fun, maybe?"Refugee B"Otherwise... I don't want to think like this, but... maybe the residents broke it themselves. To get an excuse for throwing us out—"Kageaki"..."Refugee B"...Haa. Now bakwaas is coming from my mouth also."Refugee B"But impossible, I cannot call it. I understand why they suspect us... this feeling I am having, probably they are having the same one."Kageaki"...Yes. Probably."Refugee B"Kya haal hai..."
ja:
景明「旧来の住民との間にトラブルがあるという
話も聞いていますが」難民Ｂ「ああ……俺達は歓迎されてないからな。
　あれこれと揉め事は起きてるよ」難民Ｂ「実を言えば、住民側あいつらの気持ちはわかる。
　自分の町にいきなり薄汚い格好した連中が
大勢なだれ込んできたら、誰だって嫌な気分
になるだろうさ」景明「……」難民Ｂ「けど俺達は他に行き場が無くてここに来た
んだ。
　出ていけと言われても、そうですかと頷け
やしない」景明「ええ」難民Ｂ「どうにか……受け入れて欲しいんだが」景明「何やら、関係を決定的に悪化させる事件が
あったとか」難民Ｂ「橋のことだな？」景明「はい」難民Ｂ「あいつらは俺達が壊したって言ってる。
　でも、やるわけがない……」難民Ｂ「ここの誰にそんな元気があるってんだ」景明「……」難民Ｂ「しかも何の得にもならないじゃないか。
　馬鹿げてるよ」景明「では、貴方は何者の犯行だと思われます？」難民Ｂ「さあなぁ。
　どこかの悪たれの悪戯じゃないのか？」難民Ｂ「でなければ……考えたくはないが……
　住民側が俺達を追い出す口実作りに自分で
壊した、なんてことも――」景明「……」難民Ｂ「……ふぅ。
　俺も馬鹿なこと言ってるな」難民Ｂ「でも、有り得ないとは思えないんだ。
　向こうが俺達を疑うのもわかるよ……要は
今の俺と同じ気持ちなんだろう」景明「……そうですね。おそらく」難民Ｂ「やれやれ、だ」

en: He looked away with a bitter smile. There was no energy left in that smile.
ja:
視線を逸らして、彼は苦笑した。
　疲れ切った笑みだった。

en:
Noon.

I went back to Hikari's house with food, and ate my own meal there as well. Nothing grand. Food had arrived, that was the main qualification of the food.

Our little host seemed genuinely pleased, just as she had in the morning. Naturally, that pleased me. Then my mind, unable to leave one decent feeling standing without inspecting its foundations, asked what she had been eating until now.

Arre, let the child enjoy her lunch. Yes. Certainly. But if this was cause for such happiness, what had the previous lunches been doing?

I had brought something to eat and somehow sat down with a question I could not swallow.
ja:
昼。
　再び光ひかりの家へ食料を持参し、ついでに自分の食事も
済ませる。

　大した物ではなかったが、朝と同様、家主は素直に
喜んでくれた様子であった。
　嬉しく思う一方、これまでどんな食生活だったのか
不安にもなる。

en: Muramasa"...So, in short. You want to get between the old residents and the new arrivals and make them reconcile?"Kageaki"More or less. If both sides keep collecting resentment and suspicion, sooner or later the result could be disastrous."Kageaki"I want to prevent that."Muramasa"I think it will be difficult."Kageaki"Easy, it certainly will not be."
ja:
村正「……要するに。
　昔からの住人と新しく入ってきた人達との
間を取り持って、和解させたいの？」景明「まぁ、そうだ。
　このまま互いに不満と不信の念を募らせて
いけば、やがて破滅的な結果になりかねない」景明「それを防ぐ」村正「難しいと思うけど」景明「簡単ではなかろうな」

en:
For a relationship to break, one instant is sufficient. For it to mend, sometimes even a hundred years is not sufficient. No symmetry in that arrangement.

One fellow opens his mouth: finished. Now three generations must sit together discovering the proper way to close it. By the time they agree, somebody's grandson has found a fresh thing to say.

Haan. Easy, it certainly would not be.
ja:
人間関係の決裂は一瞬で済むが、和解は百年の時を
掛けてなお成就しない場合がある。

en: Kageaki"But even I might be able to give reconciliation somewhere to start..."Muramasa"..."Kageaki"I can at least try."
ja:
景明「しかし、俺でも和解の切欠を作るくらいの
事はできるかもしれない……」村正「……」景明「やるだけはやってみる」

en:
Whatever form it had taken, I had stopped one quarrel. Then I could do it again.

Haan. One success. Already the mind was rolling up its sleeves like an experienced peacemaker. Ask it for a second example and suddenly it would need to go somewhere. Urgent work. Very far.

No. Not could. I wanted to believe I could. There was a difference, and I had nearly marched straight across it wearing shoes.

If a man like me was being kept alive, I wanted there to be some meaning in it. Something accomplished. Not merely air going in, air coming out, congratulations to the lungs. They were doing their work. I wanted to do mine.
ja:
どんな形であったにせよ、一度は争いを止められた
のだ。
　なら、今度もできる――できると信じたい。

　俺のような者が生かされるなら、生かされる意味が
欲しい。
　何かを成し遂げたい。

en: Hikari"............"Muramasa"I see. Then... what are you planning?"Kageaki"This probably will not be settled by talking alone. First, some action is needed."Kageaki"I will ask the refugees to take that action."
ja:
小光「…………」村正「そう。
　それで……どうする気なの？」景明「話し合いだけで片付く問題ではないだろう。
　まず行動が必要だ」景明「難民側に行動を起こして貰う」

en: Refugee B"The bridge...?"Kageaki"Yes."
ja: 難民Ｂ「橋を……？」景明「はい」

en:
The young man received me again, although his face was plainly asking whether I had no other place to go. Perhaps some of the suspicion had worn off: several others came out behind him this time.

My proposal took all of them by surprise. This particular madness they had not expected from me.
ja:
再度訪れた俺を、先刻の男性はまたかという表情を
しながらも迎えてくれた。
　幾らか警戒が薄れたのか、他にも数人がその後ろに
姿を現している。

　俺の言葉を聞いて、彼らは一様に虚を衝かれた様子
だった。

en: Refugee A"Rebuild the bridge, you're saying?"Kageaki"Yes. Timber and tools, I have a few connections for those. I will arrange them."Kageaki"Money is not a worry you need to take on."Refugee B"...Saying that is all very well."Refugee A"Arre, why should WE do it? We are not the ones who broke the damn bridge!"Kageaki"Yes."
ja:
難民Ａ「橋を建て直す、って」景明「そうです。
　材木や道具は自分に少々ツテがあるので、
そちらから調達します」景明「金銭面の心配は要りません」難民Ｂ「……と言われてもな」難民Ａ「なんで俺達がそんなことしなきゃいけない？
　あの橋を壊したのは俺達じゃないんだ！」景明「はい」

en: On that point I agreed. More than half my evidence was a feeling, admittedly. Most likely, somebody else altogether had broken the bridge.
ja:
半分以上は勘だが、その点には同意できた。
　おそらく橋を壊したのは全く別の人間だろう。

en: Kageaki"This is not rebuilding it as punishment for a wrong you did."Refugee A"Then what is it for?"Kageaki"Good faith."Refugee B"...Good faith?"Kageaki"Yes. I think you should show that you want to contribute as residents of this town, not become a burden on it."Refugee B"..."Refugee A"But WHY should we?! War drove us out, and somehow we managed to reach this place!"Refugee A"We haven't done anything wrong. After all that, more hardship we must carry?! Why, bhai, WHY?"Kageaki"...I understand how you feel. But it is also a fact that, at present, the arrival of so many people has made living conditions worse for those already here."Refugee A"..."Kageaki"You are not at fault. Neither are the residents."Kageaki"If both sides plant themselves on 'I have done nothing wrong' and refuse to move, the problem also will not move. There must be some giving way on both sides."Kageaki"And—"Refugee B"The first ones to give way must be us."Kageaki"...Yes."Refugee A"...Tch... why..."Refugee B"Don't make yourself bitter over it. Kya karein? We are the ones who came later."Refugee B"If we want them to accept us, we have to make an effort. Put like that, it is only natural."Refugee A"..."Refugee B"If the residents keep looking at us like this... sooner or later, out we go. After that, we can only die by the roadside."Refugee B"But if we manage to make peace with them—"Kageaki"That will carry considerable weight with the authorities and the police. It will be one reason for them to favour accepting and protecting you."
ja:
景明「贖罪として再建するのではありません」難民Ａ「じゃあ、何のために」景明「誠意です」難民Ｂ「……誠意？」景明「はい。
　この町の厄介者になるのではなく、住民と
なって貢献する意欲を示すべきと考えます」難民Ｂ「…………」難民Ａ「それこそ、なんでだ！
　俺達は戦に逐われてようやくここまで辿り
着いただけなんだぞ!?」難民Ａ「何も悪いことはしてねえ。
　なのになんで、この上そんな苦労を背負い
込まないとならないんだ……！」景明「……お気持ちは理解できます。
　しかし、貴方がたが流入した事で、現在の
ところ旧来の住民の生活環境が悪化している
のも事実なのです」難民Ａ「……」景明「貴方がたに罪は無い。
　住民側もそれは同じ」景明「双方が自分は悪くないと意地を張り合って
いる限り、問題は解決しません。
　譲歩し合う必要があります」景明「そして――」難民Ｂ「先に譲歩するのは、俺達か」景明「……はい」難民Ａ「……ッ……なんで……」難民Ｂ「腐るなよ。
　それは仕方ない。俺達は後から来たんだ」難民Ｂ「受け入れて貰うために努力が必要ってのは、
当然と言えば当然の話だ」難民Ａ「……」難民Ｂ「このまま住民に睨まれ続ければ……いずれ
俺達は追い出される。
　そうなったら、野垂れ死にするしかない」難民Ｂ「けれど、うまく住民側と和解できれば――」景明「その事実は行政や警察の判断にも強く影響
するでしょう。
　受け入れ、保護する方向へ方針が傾く一因
となります」

en: In his official capacity, the chief of Kamakura police was not a man whose heart would melt on demand. Still, if good relations with the residents were an established fact, he surely would not brush that aside when deciding what to do about the refugees.
ja:
鎌倉署長は公人として必ずしも甘い温情家ではない。
　が、難民対策を決めるに当たって、もし『住民との
良好な関係』という一事実があるのなら、決して軽視
はしない筈だった。

en: Refugee A"...So if we rebuild the bridge, they'll accept us?"Kageaki"That guarantee I cannot give."Refugee A"Very dependable, this..."Kageaki"I am sorry. What I can promise is to work toward getting them to accept you."Refugee A"..."Refugee B"And the bridge-building is only us?"Kageaki"Yes. I will help, but... I don't think we should bring in outside workers."Kageaki"Contractors would cost money. Besides, if somebody else does the rebuilding, the whole point is lost."Refugee B"That is true."Refugee A"Oi... You're actually going to do it?"Refugee B"...Yes. It's not as if my hands are occupied."Refugee B"You also get a day's labour once a week, if that, no?"Refugee A"..."Refugee B"Perhaps doing it will achieve nothing. But doing nothing, we are already wasting the time. Might as well try the one that has some chance."Refugee A"..."Refugee A"Maybe..."Kageaki"Then you will do it?"Refugee B"Yes. Count me in. I'll ask the younger fellows as well."Refugee B"But I don't think many will come... don't set your hopes too high."Kageaki"That is quite all right. Thank you for your help."
ja:
難民Ａ「……あの橋を建て直せば、住民側は俺達を
認めるのか？」景明「確約は致しかねます」難民Ａ「あてにならねえ……」景明「申し訳ありません。
　自分にお約束できるのは、認められるよう
働き掛ける事だけです」難民Ａ「……」難民Ｂ「橋造りは俺達だけで？」景明「はい。
　自分はお手伝いしますが……外部に人手を
求めるべきではないでしょう」景明「業者を頼むには金が掛かりますし、それに
他人の手で建て直しても意味がありません」難民Ｂ「確かにそうだな」難民Ａ「おい……やるつもりなのか？」難民Ｂ「……ああ。
　どうせ体は空いてるんだ」難民Ｂ「お前だって、日雇い仕事が週に一度あるか
無いかだろう」難民Ａ「…………」難民Ｂ「やっても無駄かもしれないが……やらなく
たって無駄に時間を過ごすだけなんだ。
　だったら、いくらかは見込みのありそうな
方を試してみてもいい」難民Ａ「……」難民Ａ「かもな……」景明「やって頂けますか」難民Ｂ「ああ。俺は乗るよ。
　若い連中にも声を掛けてみる」難民Ｂ「ただ、そんなには集まらないと思う……。
　あまり期待しないでくれ」景明「結構です。
　宜しくお願いします」

en: Muramasa"Seems that went well."Kageaki"For the moment."Muramasa"But even a small river like this—putting a bridge across it is quite a job, no?"Kageaki"I think so too. If only someone has worked as a carpenter..."Muramasa"Am I allowed to help?"Kageaki"...No. Not that."Muramasa"Thought so."
ja:
村正「うまくいったようね」景明「ひとまずはな」村正「けれど、こんな小川でも橋を架けるのって
わりあい大変なんじゃない？」景明「俺もそう思う。
　大工の経験者がいれば良いのだが……」村正「私は手伝ってもいいの？」景明「……いや。
　それは無しだ」村正「やっぱり」

en:
Muramasa was not a carpenter, but she could use a tsurugi's extraordinary abilities. For rebuilding a bridge, those would certainly be useful.

Very good. And how was I to explain them to the men working with me?

This is my companion. Please do not be alarmed if she performs one small impossibility. She is very helpful. Haan, the timber has moved by itself. Kindly concentrate on the spirit of cooperation.

An ordinary policeman was not supposed to own a tsurugi. We were trying to remove suspicion, not give everybody a new and much more interesting thing to be suspicious about.

If I forced some explanation onto the matter, our hard-won agreement might float away before we had even put anything across the river.
ja:
村正は大工ではないが、劒冑の異能を行使できる。
　橋の再建に役立つ事は間違いないだろう。
　
　しかし、作業仲間にどう説明したものか。

　一介の警官が劒冑を持つ筈はない。
　強引に言い繕えば不審を買い、折角まとまった話も
水泡に帰す恐れがある。

en: Kageaki"There is something else I would like you to do."Muramasa"What?"
ja: 景明「お前には別件を頼みたい」村正「なに？」

en:
The materials were obtained without difficulty. The very next day, we began work.

Total strength: six people. A few more pairs of hands would have been welcome, but demanding luxuries would not produce them.

First, inspect the site.
ja:
資材の調達は滞りなく済んだ。
　その翌日、早速作業を開始する。

　集まった人員は総勢六人。
　本当はもう少し手が欲しいところだったが、贅沢を
言っても仕方ない。

　まずは現場の検分から始める。

en: Kageaki"As I thought... it is deep."Refugee B"Around the middle, we'd be in up to the waist."Kageaki"Some places may be deeper still."
ja: 景明「やはり……深い」難民Ｂ「真ん中辺りは腰まで沈みそうだな」景明「もっと深い場所もあるかもしれません」

en:
After only a few minutes in the water, I understood why children did not play here. The river was not suitable for that kind of optimism.

It was deep, the bed was soft mud, and the current was fast. Given those conditions, it was no wonder that nobody had put together a temporary floating bridge, important though this crossing was.
ja:
川に入ってみてほんの数分で、ここが子供の遊び場
にされていない理由は察しがついた。
　危険過ぎるのだ。

　深い上に川底はぬかるみ、しかも流れは速い。
　重要な橋というわりに即席の浮橋を仕立てて代用に
する様子がないのも、この川並なら当然だった。

en: Refugee B"I knew it wouldn't be easy, but..."Kageaki"Has anyone here built a bridge before?"Refugee A"...No..."Refugee B"...Not many people have, I imagine. Just to check, what about you?"Kageaki"No experience. I have done construction work, but a bridge..."Refugee A"Wah. We've barely started and already the difficulties are lined up to welcome us..."Refugee B"...Well, the river isn't very wide. Even amateurs ought to manage something."Kageaki"Yes. It may take some time."Refugee A"..."Refugee B"First let's try, na?"Refugee A"...Fine. Complaining alone isn't going to start the work."
ja:
難民Ｂ「楽じゃないのはわかってたが……」景明「何方か、橋を建てた経験のある方はおられ
ますか？」難民Ａ「……いや……」難民Ｂ「……それは中々いないだろう。
　一応確かめるが、あんたは？」景明「未経験です。
　建築業に関わった事はありますが……橋と
いうのは」難民Ａ「いきなり前途多難じゃねえか……」難民Ｂ「……まっ、川幅は大したことないんだ。
　素人でも何とかならないことはないだろう」景明「はい。
　時間は掛かるかもしれませんが」難民Ａ「……」難民Ｂ「まずはやってみるさ。な？」難民Ａ「……わかったよ。
　文句ばっか言ってても始まらないしな」

en: Resident A"...? Oi, officer. What is today's activity? Standing in the river like that."Resident B"Drunk again, are you?"Kageaki"No. We are surveying the site to rebuild the bridge."Resident B"Rebuild it? You?"Resident B"With this lot?"Refugee A"..."Resident A"Hah! Good. So the police do get things done."Resident A"Made the bridge-breakers admit it, and now they're paying for it. Very good."Refugee A"Kya bola?!"Refugee B"Leave it..."Kageaki"No. That is not what is happening. These people had nothing to do with the bridge being destroyed."Kageaki"They are not working under my orders, either. They have simply decided to rebuild it out of goodwill."Resident A"Goodwill, is it...? Hm. If you say so."Refugee A"..."Resident A"Anyway, fine by me. They break it, they fix it. Why would I interfere?"Resident A"You fellows work hard now."Refugee A"...Tch..."Refugee B"..."
ja:
住民Ａ「……？
　おい、今日は何やってんだよお巡り。川に
浸かったりして」住民Ｂ「また酔っ払ってんのか？」景明「いえ。
　橋を建て直すため、調査をしているところ
です」住民Ｂ「橋を建て直す？
　あんたが？」住民Ｂ「そいつら使ってか」難民Ａ「…………」住民Ａ「はッ。そりゃあいい。
　警察も結構やってくれるじゃねえか」住民Ａ「橋を壊した奴らに罪を認めさせて、償いを
させてるってわけだ」難民Ａ「何だと!?」難民Ｂ「止せよ……」景明「それは違います。
　この方々と橋の破壊とは関係ありません」景明「また、自分に命令されて働いているのでも
ありません。
　単に善意から橋の再建を思い立ってくれた
だけです」住民Ａ「善意ね……。
　どうだかね」難民Ａ「…………」住民Ａ「まぁいいさ。
　てめぇで壊したもんをてめぇで直すってん
なら邪魔することもねえ」住民Ａ「せいぜい頑張ってやりな」難民Ａ「……っ……」難民Ｂ「……」

en:
The two men left. Perhaps their visit had started it: the other residents nearby were now directing their attention toward us.

Not warm attention. No danger of anybody overheating from this welcome.

Naturally. Once ill feeling has settled in, it does not vacate the place so easily. For now, we could only try not to mind it. Later I would find a quiet way to say as much to the others.
ja:
二人連れは去っていった。
　しかし彼らが契機となったのか、周辺の住民達から
視線が集まり始めている。

　温かくはない。冷淡と言っていい。
　さもあろう――一度抱かれた悪感情は、そう簡単に
覆らないものだ。

　ひとまず気にせずにおくしかない。
　後でそれとなく皆に言っておこう。

en: Old Man"..."Old Man"...Hmph..."

Several days went by in a flash. The work had declined to accompany them at that speed.

To speak plainly, progress was painfully slow. We were a collection of amateurs; what else could one expect? Even so, the foundations were finally beginning to take shape.
ja:
数日は瞬く間に過ぎたが、過ぎた時間に見合うほど
作業は進んでいなかった。
　有体に言えば、遅々としている。

　素人集団のやる事であるから仕方ない。
　それでも、基部は漸ようよう出来上がりつつあった。

en: Refugee B"So we do need girders, after all?"Refugee A"We can't just lay planks across the foundations and declare the bridge finished."Kageaki"Yes. There would be a safety problem."Refugee B"Then should we give it a leg in the middle also?"Kageaki"That... well..."
ja:
難民Ｂ「やっぱり橋桁はしげたは要るか」難民Ａ「土台の上に板を渡して終わりってわけにも
いかないだろ」景明「は。安全性に問題があります」難民Ｂ「なら、真ん中に脚・も造るか？」景明「それは……さて……」

en:
From the width of the river, it seemed we could do without one. But with one, the bridge would probably be steadier.

Materials, at least, we still had to spare.
ja:
川幅を見るに、不要とも思える。
　しかし、あった方が安定感は高まりそうだ。

　資材にはまだゆとりがある。

en: Kageaki"Perhaps we should build one and see."Refugee A"Yes. It shouldn't get in the way."Refugee B"Once the abutments are ready, then."Kageaki"Yes."
ja:
景明「造るだけ造ってみても良いかと」難民Ａ「そうだな。
　邪魔にはならないだろうし」難民Ｂ「橋台きょうだいが出来たらやるか」景明「ええ」

en: Old Man"..."Old Man"Ah... Oi..."Kageaki"Yes? What is it?"
ja: 老人「…………」老人「あー……おい……」景明「？　は、何でしょう」

en:
I thought someone had called quietly, and turned. Sure enough, an old man stood there, watching us with a pipe in his mouth. His clothes were not those of a refugee.

No smoke was coming out. The pipe, it seemed, was empty.
ja:
小声で呼ばれたように思えて振り返ると、果たして
そこには老人が一人いた。
　難民の服装ではない。煙管を咥えてこちらを眺めて
いる。

　煙が立っていないところを見ると、中身は空っぽの
ようだ。

en: Old Man"..."Kageaki"...Uncle?"Old Man"...No..."Old Man"Nothing. No need for me to interfere."Kageaki"...?"
ja: 老人「…………」景明「……御老人？」老人「……いや……」老人「何でもねえ。余計なこった」景明「……？」

en:
...A little rain had started, it seemed.

Perhaps because the walls were thin, even that light rain made itself heard very clearly.

Since work on the bridge began, I had been staying at Hikari's house. Outskirts or not, this was still Kamakura. Coming from the chief's house every day would have been no trouble. Still, I had my reasons for staying here.

For my host, I brought food and other necessities in return. In these times, and for a child living alone, cash was not necessarily the most useful form of thank-you. This seemed better.
ja:
……少し、降り始めたようだ。
　
　壁が薄いからか、小雨の音がよく響く。

　橋の再建を始めてよりこのかた、俺は光ひかりの家で厄介
になっている。
　外れとはいえ鎌倉市内。署長宅から通うに不都合は
無いのだが――理由あってこうしていた。

　家主への返礼は食料ほか生活必需品である。
　今の時勢そして子供の一人暮らしという事情を思う
に、現金よりこの方が良かろうと考えたのだ。

en: Kageaki"..."

Once, I had asked whether she would like to come and live with me. Not even a little hesitation in the answer.

Hikari shook her head. She would wait here for her mother to return.

After that, I did not bring it up again.

Her mother had disappeared without warning, she said. The chance of her coming back was almost nothing—or so I thought. Dead, of course she would not return. But even alive, probably not.

That did not mean I should say all this and persuade Hikari to agree with me. What good would that do her? None that I could see. So I kept my mouth closed.

She appeared to be alone. But for her, the family was still there. As long as she believed it, still there. On the strength of my own judgment, I had no right to take that away.

Being kind did not give me permission to march across the distance between us. We were strangers; respecting that distance was what I could do for her. Leave her sanctuary alone.

From the other side of that distance, Hikari was now watching me. What was in those eyes, I could not quite read.
ja:
一度、一緒に暮らさないかと持ち掛けてみた。
　その返答は迷いなく。

　ここで母の帰りを待つからと、光は首を横に振った。
　
　以来、その話はしていない。

　前触れもなく姿を消したという母親が戻る見込みは
皆無に近い――そう思う。
　死んでいれば当然、生きていてもだ。

　しかし、そこまで口にして光を説き伏せるべきとは
思われなかった。それは全く彼女にとって良い事では
ないと思えた。
　だから俺は口を噤んだ。

　彼女は独りきりに見える。
　だが家族はまだいる・・・・のだ――彼女がそう信じる限り。
俺の独断でそれを取り上げて良い筈はない。

　俺にできる親切とは、他人同士の距離を踏み越える
事ではなく守る事であった。彼女の聖域を侵さぬよう。
　その距離から今、光は俺に不分明な眼差しを注いで
いる。

en: Kageaki"...? Is there something?"Hikari"Kageaki..."Hikari"Why are you trying so hard?"Kageaki"—"
ja: 景明「……？　何か？」小光「かげあきは……」小光「どうして、がんばるの？」景明「――――」

en:
Such a small question. No difficulty understanding what she meant, though: my going to the refugees and trying to rebuild the bridge with them.

Had she watched the whole thing? Or had she understood without needing to see, with some strange sense that grown-ups did not possess? Somehow she knew I was trying.
ja:
言葉足らずの問い掛けは、それでも意味明瞭だった。
　問われているのは、難民を語らって橋の建て直しを
試みる俺の振舞いだ。

　彼女は一部始終を見ていたのか。
　それとも見るまでもなく、大人にはない不可思議な
感性で俺が頑張っている・・・・・・事を悟ったのか。

en: Hikari"Why?"Kageaki"...Ah. That is... I want everyone to get along."Hikari"Get along?"Kageaki"Yes."Hikari"Why?"
ja:
小光「どうして？」景明「……は。それは……
　みんなに仲良くして欲しいからです」小光「なかよく？」景明「はい」小光「どうして？」

en:
Again, why.

I went through the words in my head, looking for suitable ones.

...Whether these were suitable, I did not know.
ja:
繰り返しの疑問。
　俺は脳裏で言葉を選んだ。

　……適切かどうかわからないが……

en: Kageaki"Harmony is to be valued."Hikari"Harmy?"Kageaki"Harmony."Hikari"Harmony."Kageaki"Is to be valued."Hikari"Is to be val-yood."Kageaki"Yes."Hikari"...What's that?"Kageaki"Something a great person said long ago. Getting along with each other is important—that is what he was saying."Kageaki"If we only go on fighting, nothing gets done. If we help each other instead, anything can be done... that is why."Hikari"Anything?"Kageaki"Yes. Growing food, building houses..."Hikari"A zoo also?"Kageaki"That can be done."Hikari"A movie theatre?"Kageaki"That too can be done."Hikari"Amazing..."Kageaki"Yes. But—"Kageaki"If we don't get along, if we keep fighting, not only do we fail to build those things. Sometimes we destroy them also."Hikari"That's bad..."Kageaki"Yes."Hikari"Then how do we stop fighting and get along?"Kageaki"..."
ja:
景明「和を以て貴しとす」小光「わお？」景明「和を以て」小光「わをもって」景明「貴しとす」小光「とぉとしとす」景明「はい」小光「……なぁに？」景明「昔の偉い人が言った言葉です。
　仲良くする事を大切にしなさい――」景明「争ってばかりいては何もできない。
　争わず、助け合えば、どんな事でもできる
から……と」小光「どんなことでも？」景明「はい。
　食べる物を育てたり、家を建てたり」小光「どうぶつえんは？」景明「できます」小光「えいがかんは？」景明「できます」小光「すごい……」景明「はい。
　ですが――」景明「仲良くせず、争っていると、そうした物は
作れないばかりか、壊してしまうこともあり
ます」小光「だめ……」景明「はい」小光「あらそわないで、なかよくするには、どう
したらいいの？」景明「…………」

en: Kageaki"The way you did, before."Hikari"...?"Kageaki"You gave someone your own food. Because you thought he was having more difficulty than you."Kageaki"...It sounds a small thing. Doing it is not small. When they have enough for themselves, many people can be kind to others. When they themselves are suffering, very few can still do it."Kageaki"When things become difficult, people think only of protecting themselves. Sometimes they even take from others to save themselves... You did not do that."Hikari"..."Kageaki"What you did was a very fine thing."Hikari"...Oh..."
ja:
景明「貴方が以前、して下さったように」小光「？」景明「貴方は自分の食べ物を人に与えました。
　自分よりも困っているから、と」景明「……簡単なようで難しい事です。
　自分に余裕がある時、他人に優しくできる
人は多くいる――しかし自分が苦しい時にも
そうできる人は少ない」景明「自分が苦しいと、人は自分だけを守り、時
には他人から奪って自分を救おうとさえする。
　……貴方はそうではなかった」小光「…………」景明「とても立派な事です」小光「……そう……」

en:
Perhaps praise was not something she was used to receiving. Hikari lowered her head shyly.

Pink had come into her cheeks, like peaches.
ja:
褒められる事に慣れていないのか。
　光ははにかんで、俯いた。

　頬に朱が差して、桃のようになっている。

en: Kageaki"...If everyone cared for others before themselves, there would be no quarrels."Kageaki"That would be... a very good thing."Hikari"...Yes."Hikari"It would be nice, na? If it became like that."Kageaki"..."
ja:
景明「…………。
　誰もが自分の事より他人の事を思いやれば、
争いなど起きません」景明「それは……とても良い事です」小光「……うん」小光「そうなると、いいね」景明「…………」

en:
So that was that.

By yesterday evening, we had somehow finished the bridge's foundations. Not a handsome job, but finished. This morning, a beaver's lodge stood in their place. The collapse was so complete that nobody looking at it would suspect we had ever intended a bridge.

One look gave the likely reason. The river had risen in the rain; our work had apparently not been equal to this small disagreement.
ja:
あっさりしたものであった。

　昨日の夕、不恰好ながらもどうにか仕上がっていた
橋の土台は、一夜明けた今、海狸ビーバーの巣に変貌している。
　見事なまでの倒壊ぶりだった。これを見て、ここに
橋を建てる構想があったと思う者はいまい。

　倒壊の所以は一見して明らかだ。
　雨による増水に耐えられなかったのだろう。

en: Refugee B"..."Refugee A"..."

My fellow builders stared down at the wreckage without a word. Even for speaking, they seemed to have no energy left.

My own condition was not very different.

We stood in a row like stone Jizo statues while the neighbours passed behind us. Now and then, somebody made sure we received a laugh at our expense.

...We had been too optimistic.

The biggest mistake was probably that the foundation piles were too shallow. We had considered the soft riverbed and driven them deep—or what we had generously decided was deep. It had not been enough.

Other faults came to mind also. Most were things we had noticed while working, then collectively settled with 'probably all right.' Such excellent agreement we had achieved over our mistakes.

We should have taken more care...
ja:
橋造りの仲間は、黙って惨状を眺め下ろしている。
　声を出す気力もない様子だった。

　俺もほぼ同様だ。

　石地蔵となって立ち並ぶ背後を、近隣に住む人々が
行き交う。
　時折、聞こえよがしな嘲笑が届いた。

　……見立てが甘かった。

　最大の失敗は、基礎となる杭の浅さだろう。
　川底の軟弱さを考慮して深くまで打ち込んだつもり
だったが、まだ足りなかったのだ。

　他にも思い当たる節はある。
　その多くは、作業中から既に気付きつつもおそらく
大丈夫だろうと皆で楽観し、見過ごしにしてしまった
事柄だ。

　もっと慎重に工事をするべきだった……。

en: Kageaki"First, let us put the problems in order."Refugee A"..."Kageaki"After that, we start again from the design—"Refugee B"..."Kageaki"..."
ja: 景明「まずは問題点を整理しましょう」難民Ａ「……」景明「その上で設計からやり直し――」難民Ｂ「……」景明「…………」

en:
No answer. Only that heavy sense of wasted effort coming out with their breath.

I could hardly blame them. Yes, we had accepted that the work might achieve nothing. Seeing it actually, completely achieve nothing was a different matter. Who would not lose heart?

I could not think of a way to encourage them, either.

...For now, at least, recover the wreckage.

I stepped into the river and took hold of the timber. It had gone into avant-garde art without consulting us.
ja:
誰も返答しない。
　俺の言葉に応えるのは、彼らが呼吸と共に吐き出す
濃い徒労感だけだった。

　無理もない話だ。
　報われず、無駄に終わる事も覚悟の上での作業では
あったが、本当に全く無駄になったのを見て落胆せず
にいられるものではないだろう。

　俺としても励ます方法が思いつかない。
　……とりあえず、残骸の回収を始めておくとしよう。

　俺は川へ踏み込み、前衛芸術化している材木に手を
掛けた。

en: Old Man"Arre... bas, yaar."Old Man"I cannot watch this anymore."Kageaki"...?"
ja: 老人「あぁー……ったく」老人「見てられねえ」景明「……？」

en: The sudden voice belonged to yesterday's old man. Pipe in his mouth again, still doing nothing but looking like a pipe, he came striding straight toward us.
ja:
不意の声は、昨日の老人だった。
　今日も格好だけ煙管を咥えつつ、こちらへずかずか
と歩いてくる。

en: Old Man"Oi."Kageaki"Yes."Old Man"All of you are complete amateurs, correct?"Kageaki"Yes... None of us has built a bridge before."Old Man"Not even one carpenter among the whole lot."Kageaki"Your assessment is correct."Old Man"And you decided to build a bridge? Wah. No carpentry, no experience, straight to arguing with a bloody RIVER. Like doing stand-up without a mouth."Kageaki"...It is that difficult?"Old Man"I'm retired now. Used to be a carpenter. Built a few bridges also."Old Man"A house stands on ground that stays put. A bridge has to get along with a river that keeps moving. Much more trouble, that."Kageaki"...I see."
ja:
老人「おい」景明「はい」老人「おめぇら、全員素人トーシロだな」景明「は……
　誰も橋を建てた経験は有りません」老人「大工やってた奴すらいねえだろう」景明「お察しの通りです」老人「それでよく橋を造ろうなんて考えたな。
　口の利けねえ奴が漫才やるようなもんだ」景明「……そこまで困難な事ですか」老人「おれは隠居してるが、昔は大工だ。
　橋を造ったことも何度かある」老人「動かない地面の上に建てる家より、流れる
川と付き合わなきゃいけねえ橋は余計に面倒
だったさ」景明「……成程」

en:
Perhaps that was how it was. Perhaps a group of amateurs doing the whole thing alone had been an unreasonable idea from the start.

Only now this possibility was presenting itself to me...
ja:
そういうものかもしれない。
　素人だけでやろうとしたのがそもそも無理だったと
いう事か……。

en: Kageaki"Uncle."Old Man"Hm?"Kageaki"You were a carpenter, and you have built bridges. Could we ask for your help?"Old Man"..."Kageaki"Even advice would be enough. Please—"Old Man"If I didn't mean to help, why would I have opened my mouth?"Kageaki"Then—"Old Man"YOU FELLOWS OVER THERE!"Refugee B"...?"Refugee A"Eh?"Old Man"From now on, do what I tell you. First, clear away that rubbish."Refugee B"..."Refugee A"..."Old Man"Arre, move, you bloody statues! Bridge banana hai, na?! You want to build the damn bridge or not?!"Refugee B"Ah..."Refugee A"Y-yes..."
ja:
景明「御老人」老人「ん？」景明「元大工で、しかも橋造りの経験者でもあら
れる貴方の力をお貸し願えませんか」老人「…………」景明「助言して下さるだけで良いのです。
　どうか――」老人「その気がなけりゃ、声掛けたりしねえよ」景明「では」老人「そっちのおめぇら！」難民Ｂ「……？」難民Ａ「え？」老人「今からおれの言う通りに動け。
　まず、そのガラクタを片付けるんだ」難民Ｂ「……」難民Ａ「……」老人「ぼさっとしてんじゃねえ！
　橋を造るんだろうが！」難民Ｂ「あ……」難民Ａ「お、おう……」

en: Kageaki"Then we make the foundations like this... And a leg in the middle?"Old Man"For this much river? No need. It'll only catch rubbish. Better without."Old Man"Put that effort into proper abutments."Kageaki"Yes. Understood."Resident A"...? Kume uncle? What are you doing?"Resident B"Helping this lot, are you?"Old Man"Something like that. You two have the day off?"Resident B"Yes, but..."Old Man"Then lend a hand."Resident A"Huh? Arre, why should we do—"Old Man"Bas, stop the bakbak. Without this bridge you're having trouble, no?"Resident A"Well... yes, but—"Old Man"Leave it all to these fellows and you can wait till your bones become timber. Still no bridge."Resident B"..."Old Man"Go change. Quickly. And if anyone else is sitting idle, bring them along."Resident B"...What do we do?"Resident A"What do you mean, what do we do? ...No choice, is there?"Resident A"Bloody hell. Against this old man, no chance."
ja:
景明「では、土台はこのようにするとして……
　脚は？」老人「この川幅でそんなの要らねえよ。
　ゴミを引っ掛けるだけ、無い方がマシだ」老人「そのぶん橋台きょうだいをしっかり作っとけ」景明「は、諒解しました」住民Ａ「……？
　粂くめの爺さんじゃねえか。何やってんだ」住民Ｂ「そいつらを手伝ってるのか？」老人「まぁな。
　おめぇら、今日は休みか」住民Ｂ「そうだけど……」老人「なら手を貸せ」住民Ａ「はァ？
　おいおい、なんで俺達がそんなこと」老人「ぐだぐだ抜かすな。
　どうせここの橋は無いと困るんだろうが」住民Ａ「そりゃ……そうだが」老人「こいつらに任せてたらいつまで待ってても
出来ねえぞ」住民Ｂ「…………」老人「さっさと着替えてきな。
　あと、他にも暇な奴がいたら連れて来い」住民Ｂ「……どうする？」住民Ａ「どうもこうも。
　…………仕方ねえだろう」住民Ａ「まったく、爺さんには敵わねえ」

en: Kageaki(...Well...)
ja: 景明（……何とも……）

en:
This, I had not expected.

The established residents and the newly arrived refugees were working side by side. Helping each other to build one thing.

Not that they had made peace. Let me not become a great statesman merely because six fellows had picked up some wood.

They exchanged no words and no smiles. When their eyes met, the looks were cold. Their distrust was still very much present.

Even so.

When heavy timber had to be carried.
When piles had to be driven into the riverbed.

One man would help another with work too much for a single pair of hands. And sometimes, one was a resident and the other a refugee.

The timber, at least, was very fair-minded. Pick it up from one end only, it would make trouble. Whatever opinion you had of the fellow at the other end, for now you needed his hands.
ja:
予想せぬ光景だった。

　旧来の住民と新参の難民が、共に立ち働いている。
　一つのものを造るため――協力して。

　彼らは和解してはいない。

　言葉を交わす事はなく、笑顔を向け合う事もない。
　時折交差する視線は冷たく、相手への不信感を隠し
切れていない。

　それでも。
　
　――重い材木を担ぎ出す時。
　――川底へ杭を打ち込む時。

　一人では手に余る作業を、別の一人が手伝い、その
両者が住民同士でも難民同士でもない事がある。

en: Kageaki(If this continues...)
ja: 景明（これならば）

en:
Time, it would take. And there would be plenty of difficulties.

But one day—
ja:
時間は掛かるだろう。
　障害は多いだろう。

　だが、いずれ――――

en: Resident B"Shouldn't we take this to the site as well?"Resident A"Yes..."
ja: 住民Ｂ「これも現場に運んだ方がいいんじゃないか」住民Ａ「そうだな……」

en: Resident A"Hm?"Resident A"Oh. It's you."Resident B"About what we discussed the other day? Sorry, but we've decided not to hire your lot. We don't have the money to pay."
ja:
住民Ａ「ん？」住民Ａ「なんだ、あんたか」住民Ｂ「こないだの話かい？
　悪いけどさ、あんたらには頼まないことに
決まったよ。払う金がないもんでね」

en: Resident B"...Huh?"Resident A"What? What did you say...?"
ja:
住民Ｂ「……はぁ？」住民Ａ「何？
　何だって……？」

en: Kageaki"Would a width sufficient for one person be all right?"Old Man"A little more. Enough for two people to pass... then a cart can use it also."Kageaki"That would certainly help. But the materials may not be enough."Old Man"Don't worry about that. If it comes to it, I'll speak to my old workplace."Kageaki"...I am putting you to a great deal of trouble."Old Man"Heh."
ja:
景明「橋の広さは、人間一人が通れる程度で良い
のでしょうか」老人「もう少しあった方がいいな。
　二人がすれ違えるくらいに……そうすりゃ
荷車も通れる」景明「それは確かに便利です。
　しかし、資材が足りないかもしれません」老人「心配すんな。
　いざとなりゃあ、おれが昔の仕事場に掛け
合ってやるよ」景明「……御造作を掛けます」老人「へッ」

en: Resident B"..."Resident A"..."Resident B"...That dopey-looking young fellow...?"Resident A"Can't be... can it?"
ja: 住民Ｂ「……」住民Ａ「……」住民Ｂ「……あのとっぽい兄ちゃんが……？」住民Ａ「まさか……なぁ？」

en: Muramasa《————Mido.》
ja: 村正《――――御堂》

en: Kageaki"Muramasa?"
ja: 景明「村正？」

en:
The middle of the night.

At the sudden metallic voice, I sprang up.

My mind was already awake. This was precisely what I had been waiting for. Hikari's house was close to the bridge site; that was why I had asked to stay there.

Muramasa, who should be at the fire-watch tower, continued her message.
ja:
夜半。
　不意の金打声に跳ね起きる。

　意識は既に覚醒していた。
　――これあるを期して、橋の現場から程近い光の家
を宿に借りたのだ。

　火見櫓ひのみやぐらにいる筈の村正が、続けて通信を送ってくる。

en: Muramasa《Seems your prediction was right. Some sneaking and fiddling has started at the worksite.》Kageaki"Understood. I am coming now."
ja:
村正《貴方の予測、的中みたいよ。
　工事の場所でごそごそ・・・・やり始めた》景明「わかった。
　すぐに行く」

en: Getting dressed would take no time. That much sense I had kept: I was already dressed to move.
ja:
身支度に掛ける時間は必要なかった。
　元々、動ける格好だ。

en: Hikari"…Nnh…?"

Kageaki"Can you tell how many?"Muramasa《Four.》Kageaki"That many I can hold off... Good. Ring the fire bell there."Muramasa《Are you sure?》Kageaki"Yes. Everyone needs to see what is really happening."Muramasa《Understood.》
ja:
景明「人数はわかるか？」村正《四人よ》景明「そのくらいなら抑えられるな……。
　良し、そこにある半鐘を鳴らせ」村正《いいの？》景明「ああ。
　真相を皆に知らしめる必要がある」村正《諒解》

en: Refugee A"Kya hua?! FIRE?!"Resident A"Arre, no! Don't tell me there's a bloody fire!"
ja: 難民Ａ「なんだぁ!?　火事か!?」住民Ａ「げっ、冗談じゃねえ!!」

en:
A fire without warning: there was nothing more frightening. The moment the alarm rang, the whole neighbourhood lost its sleep. People came rushing into the street.

And naturally, they saw.

The half-built bridge, now approaching completion.
Four men moving about it.

The tools in their hands. A saw, a machete, a hatchet...

And their faces. Nowhere to run, and no useful thought arriving to replace running.
ja:
突然の火事ほど恐ろしいものはない。
　半鐘の警報が響くや付近一帯の眠りは忽たちまち覚まされ、
人々は往来へ飛び出した。

　――そして、当然。
　それを目の当たりにする結果となった。

　完成が見えてきた出来かけの橋……
　その周囲に蠢く四人の男。

　彼らの手にある道具。
　鋸、鉈、手斧……。

　逃げ場を失い、呆然とする顔。

en: Resident B"You fellows..."Nogiyama Gangster"..."Kageaki"These are the gentlemen from the underworld who wanted employment keeping this neighbourhood safe?"Resident B"Y-yes."
ja:
住民Ｂ「あんたら……」野木山組「…………」景明「この地域の治安維持に雇われたがっていた、
筋・の方々ですか？」住民Ｂ「そ、そうだ」

en: That settled it. The truth, it turned out, was a very ordinary arrangement.
ja:
これで決まった。
　真相は、良くある事・・・・・だった。

en: Kageaki"As a sales pitch, this has some ethical difficulties."Nogiyama Gangster"..."Kageaki"First make the place unsafe. Then people will need you to make it safe. One cannot say there is no logic operating."Resident B"What are you saying?"Kageaki"These gentlemen destroyed the bridge. They were attempting the same thing again..."Kageaki"To drive the established residents and the refugees apart."Resident B"W-what?!"
ja:
景明「倫理的に問題のある売り込みセールスです」野木山組「…………」景明「治安回復を必要とさせるために、まず治安
を悪化させる。
　合理的発想と、言えなくはありませんが」住民Ｂ「どういうことだよ」景明「橋を壊したのはこの方々です。
　今もまた、同じ事を……」景明「旧来の住民と難民との間を裂くために」住民Ｂ「な……何だと!?」

en: Nogiyama Gangster"...Tch..."Kageaki"Presumably the plan was to make the people here into a source of funds. But in these circumstances, that is no longer possible. Please reconcile yourselves to the loss of business."Kageaki"Go home without another word. If you leave these people alone from now on, I expect neither the residents nor the refugees will insist on pursuing the matter."Kageaki"I will also ask them not to."Nogiyama Gangster"Keep your bloody favours to yourself."
ja:
野木山組「……ッ……」景明「全てはこの地域の住民を資金源として取り
込むためだったのでしょうが……こうなって
はもはや叶わぬ事です。
　お諦め下さい」景明「何も言わず、そのままお帰りを。
　そうして今後一切の手出しを控えて頂ける
なら、住民の方々も難民の方々もあえて貴方
がたの責任を問おうとはなさらぬでしょう」景明「そのように自分からも説得します」野木山組「要らん世話じゃァ」

en: Nogiyama Gangster"Those days are gone when 'Rokuhara's men' was enough to keep us fed. If we don't make ourselves a place to earn, we're finished, samjha?"Nogiyama Gangster"You say back off, and we must just back off?!"Kageaki"That is stubbornness without a useful purpose."Nogiyama Gangster"CHUP, you interfering bastard! Who asked you to stick your nose in—"Nogiyama Gangster"Fine! We'll take this territory by FORCE!"
ja:
野木山組「六波羅御雇の看板で食えた時代じゃねえ。
　稼ぎ場所を作らんことにゃあ、首も回らん
でのォ」野木山組「引けって言われて引けるかい！」景明「無意味な意地です」野木山組「やっかぁしいわ！
　余計な邪魔しくさって――」野木山組「こうなりゃ力ずくで縄張りシマにしたらァ!!」

en:
The man who appeared to be their leader drew his sword from its plain wooden scabbard. Beside him, the one holding the saw changed it for a dagger. The other two pointed their machete and hatchet at me.

Screams went up. The circle of onlookers took a step back.

...Avoid violence at all costs. That had been my intention. Apparently the time for explaining my intention was over.
ja:
四人の頭株と思われる男は佩刀の白鞘を払った。
　その両脇で、鋸を手にしていた男は短刀に持ち替え、
鉈と手斧の男はその刃先をこちらへ向ける。

　周囲で悲鳴が上がり、人の輪が一歩後退した。
　
　……荒事は何としても避けたかったが――この状況、
言っている場合ではないか。

en: Kageaki"Muramasa! Send me Kotetsu!"Muramasa《Understood!》
ja: 景明「村正、虎徹を寄越せ！」村正《諒解！》

en:
Four gangsters accustomed to violence, and me with empty hands. Not an arrangement in my favour. A tsurugi, however, would be excessive. One sword would do. No need to bring an armoured warrior to a neighbourhood argument. The bridge had suffered enough already.

I had to give them credit: even if the sudden appearance of a sword in my hand startled them, they offered no opening. Two came forward; the other two moved around to my left and right.

Four against one. The proper move was to put some distance between us and avoid being surrounded.

But not this time. I could not afford a lengthy affair. If they turned those blades on the people around us, it would be a disaster. The public had come out to watch; I could not let the demonstration start including them.

Resident or refugee, I would not let them hurt anyone.

So, no retreat. Forward.

Toward the man with the machete, ahead and to my right—
ja:
場慣れした筋者四人を相手に丸腰では少々分が悪い。
　といって劒冑は大袈裟、太刀一本が適当なところだ。
　流石と言うべきか、四人は俺の手の中に突如太刀が
現れるのを見て、仰天したとしてもそれで隙を作りは
しなかった。
　二人が前に出て、残り二人は左右に回る。

　四対一の形勢。
　ひとまず距離を取り、囲まれるのを防ぐ――それが
正手であろう。

　しかし今回、時間を掛けるべきではなかった。
　彼らが周囲の人々に刃を向ける事になっては大事だ。

　住民も難民も、絶対に傷付けさせてはならない。

　従って退かぬ。
　前へ出る。

　正面右、鉈を持った男へ――

en: Kageaki"—"
I moved toward him—◆or appeared to. In an instant I changed direction, meeting the hatchet man as he sprang in from my right.
ja:
行く、◆と見せて瞬時、向きを変え。
　右脇から食い付こうと飛び出しかけていた手斧男を
迎え撃つ。

en:
The back of my sword struck where I intended, driving his collarbone inward. Instead of a scream, a great breath burst out of him.

One man down.
ja:
峰打ちの一刀は過あやまたず、男の鎖骨を陥没させた。
　悲鳴の代わりに多量の空気を吐き出して、まず一人
が地面に倒れる。

en: Nogiyama Gangster"...You little bastard!!"
ja: 野木山組「……ガキァ!!」

en:
The shout came in fury. The very instant I looked toward it, a current of warning ran through the middle of my forehead.

A tremendous blow was coming.
Enough to settle the question of whether my body could remain in one piece—
ja:
激昂の声。
　そちらに視線を向けた刹那、額の中央に危機を知ら
せる電流が走った。

　凄まじい一撃が襲い来る。
　確実に俺の肉体を二つ割りにできる程の――

en:
My sword came up in time. Just in time.

Take this head-on and I would be overpowered. No, let it go at an angle. Turn it aside.

The killing edge slipped past my ear. It caught several hairs and tore them away.
ja:
危うく、防ぎの太刀は間に合った。
　真っ向から受け止めては押し負ける。斜めに逸らし、
受け流す。

　殺刃が耳の横を滑ってゆく。
　髪が数本巻き込まれ、引き千切られた。

en: Kageaki"...Tch!"

I turned my wrist.
Swung the sword around above my head—then drove it up beneath the man's arm.

One blow.
ja:
手首を返す。
　頭上で太刀を旋回させ――男の腋下を下方から抉る
ように。

　一撃。

en: Nogiyama Gangster"Gah?!"
ja: 野木山組「げほァ!?」

en:
I had held back to avoid a serious injury. That did not make a strike to a vital point comfortable. Even a gangster for whom giving and receiving blows was everyday business could not endure this one.

He writhed on the ground, foaming at the mouth. Presumably he had no fight left.

The leader was out as well.

Two to go—
ja:
重傷を負わせぬよう加減はした。
　それでも急所を打ち抜く痛撃である。殴り殴られが
日常茶飯の筋者であろうと耐えられる道理はない。

　のたうち回る男は泡を吹いていた。
　もはや戦う力はあるまい。

　これで首領格も脱落。

　残るは、二人――――

en:
I let out a breath and wiped away the sweat. The fighting had been short and fierce; it had taken a great deal out of both body and mind.

By a narrow margin, I was unhurt. All four gangsters lay on the ground, but none of them had a life-threatening wound either.

...A good result, I supposed. Though not having to fight would have been better than a good result from fighting.
ja:
吐息し、汗を拭う。
　短いが激しい戦闘は、俺の体力精神力を大きく消耗
させた。

　辛うじて、怪我はない。
　四人の筋者は全て地に伏しているが、こちらも命に
関わるような傷は誰も負っていない。

　……まぁ、上々の結果だろう。
　戦わずに済めばそれに越した事はなかったのだが。

en: Kageaki"Muramasa... no more of their men nearby?"Muramasa《You're all right.》
ja: 景明「村正……他に仲間はいないな？」村正《大丈夫よ》

en:
At her answer, I let the tension go out of my body. Whatever else, this matter was settled.

I did not expect residents and refugees to put their arms around each other and start laughing straightaway. Still, their relations would surely improve. One root of the conflict had been removed.
ja:
返答を受けて、体の力を抜く。
　兎も角もこれで一件落着だ。

　すぐにすぐ住民と難民が肩を組んで笑い合えるとは
思わないが、少なくとも関係の好転には繋がるだろう。
　対立の根が一つ、取り除かれたのだから。

en: Kageaki"...?"

Then I noticed the strange silence.
The people around me, watching...

What was this feeling? I could not put a name to it.

...Ah. A blade was not something to keep displaying after its work was done. Ordinary citizens, neither soldiers nor criminals, would understandably find that gleam threatening.

I told Muramasa to take Kotetsu back.
ja:
ふと、奇妙な静寂に気付いた。
　俺を見守る、周囲の――

　何とも言いようがない、そんな気配。
　
　……そうか。刃物など、用が済んでもひけらかして
おくものではない。

　軍人でも犯罪者でもない正常の市民にとって、刀剣
の光は脅威的だろう。
　俺は村正に命じ、虎徹を回収させた。

en: Resident A"It vanished...?!"Resident B"O-oi. Don't tell me... that story..."
ja:
住民Ａ「消えた……!?」住民Ｂ「お、おい。
　まさか――あの話……」

en:
...Arre. What had I done?

In my hurry, I had chosen entirely the wrong method. To ordinary eyes, the sword must simply have disappeared.

Excellent. They were confused, so I had supplied more confusion. Now I had to explain it away—somehow, something suitable—
ja:
……しまった。

　焦ってやり方を間違えた。
　今のは常人の視覚だと、太刀が消失したようにしか
見えない。

　わざわざ混乱を煽ってどうする。
　誤魔化さねば――何とか適当に、

en: Resident B"...You..."
ja: 住民Ｂ「……あんた……」

en: But one man gathered his nerve and opened his mouth before my explanation had managed to exist.
ja:
しかし。
　意を決した一人が口を開くのは、俺が弁明法を思い
つくより早かった。

en: Resident B"You..."Resident B"I heard you're a warrior. A murdering maniac who's killed so many people... I-is that... is it TRUE?!"
ja:
住民Ｂ「あんた」住民Ｂ「今までに何人も殺してきた、殺人鬼の武者
だって聞いたんだけど……
　ほ――ほっ、本当なのか!?」

en: Kageaki"...Eh?"Resident B"Anyone at all... women, children also. You killed them."Resident B"That's what... I heard..."Kageaki"—"
ja:
景明「……え？」住民Ｂ「誰でも構わず……
　女でも子供でも殺してきたって」住民Ｂ「聞いたん……だけど……」景明「――――――――」

en:
Who?

Who had told them?

That—truth.
ja:
誰が。

　誰が、教えたのだ。

　その――――真実を。

en: Refugee B"W-what are you suddenly saying?!"Resident B"N-no, I didn't believe it either, but—"Resident B"You saw just now, na! Finished off those gangsters as if it was nothing! The sword coming and going!"Resident B"Only a warrior can do such things!"Refugee B"That... yes, but..."Refugee A"R-ruko, wait! Even if this officer is a warrior... a murdering maniac? Surely not!"Refugee A"RIGHT?!"Kageaki"..."Refugee A"..."Refugee A"O-oi. Why are you keeping quiet?"Refugee A"Kuch toh bolo. Say something, please."Kageaki"..."
ja:
難民Ｂ「な……何を言い出すんだよ、いきなり！」住民Ｂ「い、いや。
　俺だって信じちゃいなかったけど」住民Ｂ「今の見たろ！
　ヤクザをあっさり片付けるし、刀は出たり
消えたりするし！」住民Ｂ「あんな真似、武者にしかできねえよ！」難民Ｂ「それは……そうだが……」難民Ａ「まっ、待てって！
　このお巡りさんがもし、武者だとしてもだ
……まさか殺人鬼ってことはないだろう！」難民Ａ「なぁっ!?」景明「…………」難民Ａ「…………」難民Ａ「お、おい。
　なんで黙ってるんだよ」難民Ａ「なんか言ってくれよ」景明「…………」

en:
Say something?

What... was there for me to say?

That I was not a murderer?

That much of a lie... I should tell?
ja:
言う？
　何を……言えるのだろう。

　自分は殺人鬼ではない、と？

　そんな……嘘を？

en: Kageaki"..."Refugee A"You... no, surely..."Refugee A"Surely you aren't really—"Kageaki"..."
ja: 景明「…………」難民Ａ「あんた……まさか」難民Ａ「まさか、本当に」景明「…………」

en:
In that instant, the air boiled.

When the gangsters drew their weapons, it had been nothing like this. Hoarse cries escaped from mouth after mouth. People leapt back as though away from a fire, making a wide space around me.

Farther away. A little farther. And when the people behind them left no room, they got in each other's way and began cursing.
ja:
――瞬間。
　
　空気が沸騰した。

　筋者が刃物を抜いた時の比ではなく。
　ひぃ――と掠れ声の呻きを口々に洩らしつつ、火の
上から飛び退くように、人々は俺を遠巻きにした。

　少しでも俺から離れようとし、後ろが閊つかえてそれが
果たせないと、互いに邪魔にし合って罵り合う。

en: Resident A"M-move, bhosdike!"Refugee A"Shut up! Stop pushing!"Resident A"What?! You lot brought that strange bastard here in the first place!"Refugee A"We don't know anything about him!"Resident B"Were you going to set him on us?!"Refugee A"I SAID WE DON'T KNOW! You lot were going to have him kill us—"
ja:
住民Ａ「どっ、どけよてめぇ！」難民Ａ「うるせえ、押すな！」住民Ａ「何だと!?
　そもそもてめぇらがあの変な男を引っ張り
込んだんだろうが！」難民Ａ「知らねえよっ！」住民Ｂ「俺達相手にけしかけるつもりだったのか!?」難民Ａ「知らねえってんだろ！
　お前らこそ、俺達を殺させるつもりで――」

en:
They were fighting.
These people, who had seemed so close to coming together.

Fighting.
Because of me only.

Fighting...
Pushing one another, clawing, hitting—
ja:
争っている。
　折角まとまるかと思えた人々が。

　争っている。
　俺が原因で。

　争っている……。
　押し合い、掻き毟り合い、殴り合って――

en: Kageaki"Stop."Kageaki"BAS! STOP IT!!"
ja: 景明「止めろ」景明「止めろぉっっ!!」

en: Kageaki"...Ah..."

Everyone went still.
Every face turned toward me.

Fear in every pair of eyes. No end to it.

A bloodstained murderer stood before them. What else should they feel?

Fear.
Fear.
Fear.
Fear.
ja:
人々が凝固する。
　一様に、俺を見詰めて。

　どの瞳にも恐怖がある。
　限りない恐れの念。

　血塗れの殺人鬼に対する、当然の感情。

　恐怖。
　恐怖。
　恐怖。
　恐怖。

en: Kageaki"Ugh..."Kageaki"UAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHH!!"
ja: 景明「うっ……」景明「うぁぁぁぁアアアアアアアアア!!」

en: Hikari"..."

...Drinking again.
Liquor with no taste. What a sensible occupation I had found for myself.

It had been impossible after all.
Settling the quarrel, building peace—none of it possible.

A man like me was never going to do such things.

...I had known that from the beginning.
For a moment, I had seen a dream. Then the dream had ended.

Bas. That was the entire story.

What remained was reality.
I could do nothing.
ja:
……また、飲んでいる。
　味のしない酒を。愚かしくも。

　やはり、無理だった。

　争いを収めるなど無理だった。
　和平を築き上げるなど無理だった。

　俺にそんな事ができる筈はなかった。

　……最初からわかっていた事だ。

　ふと、夢を見た。
　その夢が醒めた。

　それだけの話だ。

　後に残ったのは現実。
　
　――俺には、何もできない。

en: Kageaki"..."

Think about it, and the whole thing was laughable.

A murderer closes his eyes to his own past and starts giving wise advice. Don't fight. Live together peacefully. Such fine words, all coming out of this same mouth.

Heaven had not let it pass. It had stripped away the decoration and shown the truth.

I had failed to establish myself as a counterfeit saint. Exit as a clown instead.

Very funny.
ja:
思えば滑稽。

　人殺しが、自分の過去に目を瞑り――
　争うな、共存せよと、聞いた風な事を云う。

　どの口でそんな御託を吐けたやら。

　しかし天は見逃さなかった。
　虚飾を剥ぎ、真実を示した。

　いんちき聖者になり損ねた男は道化として退場した。

　嗤える。

en: Muramasa"Mido..."Kageaki"..."Muramasa"I think you did well. There is nothing for you to be ashamed of."
ja:
村正「御堂……」景明「…………」村正「貴方はよくやったと思う。
　恥じることは何もない」

en:
...Ashamed.

And how, exactly, was I supposed to avoid being ashamed? Me, of all people.

So many lives. So many precious lives I had taken. Among them, Lady Subaru and Hikaru. Even the family I should have protected.

A disgrace to being human.

I had scattered calamity across the whole world. There had been a chance to stop it—and I had failed.

A disgrace to being human.

And then...
ja:
……恥。

　何をどうして、恥じずにいられるだろう。
　この俺が。

　幾つもの――幾つもの――貴い命を奪った。
　その中には統様と光、守るべきだった家族すらいる。
　
　人としての恥だ。

　全世界に災厄を撒き散らした。
　阻止する機会はあったのに――果たせなかった。
　
　人としての恥だ。

　そして。

en: Kageaki"There is shame. More than anything else, I should be ashamed that—"Muramasa"..."Kageaki"For the crimes I committed... I have answered for nothing."
ja:
景明「恥はある。
　何よりも恥じるべきは――」村正「…………」景明「犯した罪に……
　何一つ、報いていない事」

en:
No judgment under the law. No act of atonement, nothing to make up for what I had done.

Doing nothing. Unable to do anything.

Still alive, very comfortably.
ja:
法に照らして裁かれる事もなく。
　償い、補いになるような何かを為す事もなく。

　何もせず何もできず。
　のうのうと生存する。

en: Kageaki"That is what I am ashamed of."Muramasa"..."Kageaki"...Why am I still alive...?"Kageaki"Why am I still here, alive...?"Muramasa"..."Muramasa"..."Kageaki"Why..."Kageaki"...I..."Muramasa"Tch..."Muramasa"You—"Kageaki"When I have no right even to that..."Kageaki"...Still living..."Muramasa"..."Muramasa"—B—"
ja: 景明「それが恥だ」村正「…………」景明「……何故生きている……」景明「何故生きているのだ、俺は……」村正「…………」村正「……………………」景明「何故……」景明「……俺は……」村正「くっ……」村正「この、」景明「そんな資格もないのに……」景明「……生きて……」村正「…………」村正「――え――」

en: Muramasa"BAS!!"
ja: 村正「ええい!!」

en:
Everything changed too quickly. My brain's processing capacity was not sufficient for the speed at which Muramasa had decided things should happen.

...What had she done?
Thread—steel thread?

My bottle was gone. A low table had arrived between us. A board. A box of pieces.

...Muramasa?
ja:
変転は突然過ぎ、急激過ぎた。
　脳の性能が追い付かず、情報処理が滞る。

　……何をされた？
　糸――鋼糸いと？

　村正……？

en: Muramasa"Aaah, bas! BAS!"Muramasa"Now you have made me properly angry!"Kageaki"Oi."Muramasa"You are impossible! Hopeless, helpless, beyond help—and then asking WHY no help is possible! Kya karun main, what am I supposed to DO with you?!"Kageaki"What—? No, before that, my bottle—"Muramasa"AAAAARGH!!"Kageaki"Calm down, Muramasa. ...Please, calm down."Muramasa"NO!"
ja:
村正「あっ、ああああ、もう！」村正「頭来た！」景明「おい」村正「貴方って人はーー！
　どうしてそうそこまでどうしようもなくて、
どうにもならなくて、どうにもしようがない
のよっ!!」景明「ど、どう？
　いや、それよりこの拘束を……」村正「くぁーーーっ!!」景明「落ち着け、村正。
　……落ち着いて下さい」村正「いやっ」

en: Calmness was not available.
ja: 嫌がられた。

en: Muramasa"You are allowed to be alive! Even if you can't do anything!"Muramasa"Why can't you give yourself even that much permission?!"Kageaki"I..."Muramasa"Earthworms, mole crickets, water striders! Breathing, eating mud, sucking fluids—what else are they doing? Still living with full confidence! So you also can live!"Kageaki"No. Wait."Muramasa"I am saying something very good here. Chup, listen!"Kageaki"It does not sound very good from this side."Muramasa"If you think your life has no meaning, turn the thought around! Being alive itself has meaning!"Muramasa"The sun does not do useless things. You are here, alive, right now. That means it is all right for you to be here!"Kageaki"...That is..."Muramasa"Kya? What?!"
ja:
村正「生きてたっていいじゃない！
　何もできなくたってっ」村正「なんで貴方は、その程度にすら自分を許せ
ないのよ！」景明「俺は……」村正「ミミズだってオケラだってアメンボだって、
呼吸したり泥食べたり体液吸ったりする以外
特に何もしてないけど堂々生きてるでしょ！
　だから貴方も生きてていいのよ！」景明「いや。待て」村正「今いい話してるんだから黙って聞いてっ！」景明「とてもそうは思えないのだが」村正「生きている意味がないって思うなら、逆に
考えなさい！
　こうして生きているだけで意味があるんだ、
って！」村正「お天道様は意味のないことなんてしないの。
　貴方が今、そうして生きているってことは、
それでいい・・・・・のよ！」景明「……それは……」村正「なによっ」

en:
That was sophistry.

Declare the present all right without any conditions, and the past also becomes a matter nobody needs to ask about—
ja:
詭弁だ。
　現状を無条件に肯定する事で過去をも不問に付そう
という――

en: Kageaki"...I have committed crimes. There is no uncertainty about that."Kageaki"So I must... take responsibility for those crimes..."Muramasa"Haan, haan, understood, fully understood! If somebody could take exact, complete responsibility for every single thing they ever did, what an admirable person that would be!"Muramasa"Whether YOU can become that person is a separate matter!"Kageaki"..."Muramasa"How great do you think you are?! Some extraordinary being, far above ordinary humanity?!"Kageaki"That is not..."Muramasa"The world is FULL of people who can't bear the weight of their responsibilities! They run away from some, forget some, and keep living! By your logic, none of them deserves to be alive?!"Kageaki"No..."Muramasa"Exactly! They are ordinary human beings!"Muramasa"Ordinary people make up the world. Why can't you admit you're just one person in that crowd?!"Kageaki"..."Kageaki"...But..."
ja:
景明「……俺は罪を犯している。
　これは完璧な事実だ」景明「だから、俺は……
　罪に対する責任を果たさなくてはならない
……」村正「えーえー、わかりますわかります。
　自分のしたこと全部に、きっちりちゃんと
責任を取れる人がいたらそれは立派でしょう
とも！」村正「でも貴方がそうなれるかどうかは別よ！」景明「……」村正「貴方は自分をどれほど凄いと思ってるの!?
　人並み外れて優れた傑物だって思ってる!?」景明「そうでは……」村正「この世の中、責任の重さに耐えられなくて
逃げたり忘れたりしながら生きてる人は一杯
いる！　貴方の理屈だと、そういう人達は皆
生きる価値なんか無いってわけ!?」景明「いや……」村正「そうよ！
　そんなの、単に普通の人間よ！」村正「世の中は普通の人間が集まって出来てる。
　貴方は自分が、その中の一人に過ぎないん
だって認められないの!?」景明「…………」景明「……だが……」

en:
Perhaps many people did give up on responsibilities they could not bear. But mine were not comparable. This was the guilt of mass murder.

Forget that and carry on living?

Such a cheap, contemptible way to live... I could not...
ja:
確かに責任を果たせず擲なげうつ者は多いかもしれない。
　しかし俺の負う責任は、そうした人々とは比較にも
ならないもの――大量殺人の罪だ。

　それを忘れて生きる、など。
　そんな浅ましく、卑しい真似は……

en: Muramasa"—"Muramasa"Achha. Fine. Now I understand. Words are not entering. We need a demonstration."Kageaki"What?"Muramasa"TAKE THAT!"
ja:
村正「――――」村正「あぁ、そう。わかった。
　思い知らせてあげないと駄目なのね」景明「何？」村正「とぉ！」

en: Kageaki"...Oi—"
ja: 景明「……おい――」

en:
Steel thread flashed again. Cups and bottles were removed to a corner.

The empty board remained before me. Apparently civilisation's liquid comforts had been suspended until further notice.
ja:
再び鋼糸が閃き、肌の上を鋭い感覚が這った。
　寒々としたものを覚え――それは持続する。

　服を剥ぎ取られていたのだから、当然だった。

en: Muramasa"This goes... here..."Kageaki"Wait. Just wait, will you."
ja: 村正「これで……こう……」景明「待て。いいから待て」

en: What was she intending to do with that piece?
ja: その足で、何をする気だ。

en: Muramasa"Mother told me, challenge a man like this... no way he can ignore it."Kageaki"...That ant woman..."
ja:
村正「ここを……こっ、こうしてやれば……
　反応しない男はいないって、母様が昔」景明「……あの蟻の人……」

en:
What sort of lessons had she been distributing so casually?

Muramasa made an opening move so provocative that my hand twitched toward a piece before I could stop myself.
ja:
さりげなく何を教えているのか。

　男性部分に触れられ、冷たい感覚が背筋を走る。
　びくりと戦慄わななく体を制御するのは不可能だった。

en: Muramasa"Ah! Aah! You moved!"Kageaki"...If it frightens you, don't issue the challenge."Muramasa"F-frightened? Who is frightened? Hmph! What a disgraceful performance!"Muramasa"One little move and you are b-baited! Sh-shameless! Full shameleshn—"Kageaki"First decide which word you are trying to say."
ja:
村正「わっ、わっ……動いた」景明「……おっかないなら触るな」村正「べっ、別に？
　ふ――ふふんっ、だらしない姿ねっ」村正「こんなことされて、ここを、ここここんな
風にしちゃうなんては、はず、はずかちゃっ」景明「噛み噛みで何を言ってるんだお前は」

en: Was I the drunk one here, or was it actually her?
ja: 実は酔っているのは俺ではなくこいつではないのか。

en: Muramasa"Never mind all that! I am going to make you understand!"Kageaki"Understand what?"Muramasa"That you are not some magnificent, exceptional being! You think you are too good to live basely? I will bring you down to ordinary level!"Muramasa"My little plaything, losing in a ridiculous game—AAH! That piece can go THERE?!"Kageaki"..."Muramasa"..."Muramasa"Hah. What a pathetic sight you are, Mido!"Kageaki"From here, you appear to be the one struggling desperately."Muramasa"Enjoy saying that while you can! M-men aren't built to resist this kind of competition, apparently!"Muramasa"One more move and—"
ja:
村正「いっ、いいのよ！
　とにかく、思い知らせてあげるんだから！」景明「何を」村正「貴方なんか全然たいした人間じゃないって
ことをよっ。
　卑しい生き方はできないって思ってるなら、
卑しい人間にしてあげる」村正「私の嬲りものになって、無様な姿を――
　ひゃわ!?　なんかびくっとしてるびくっと
してるこれっ!!」景明「…………」村正「…………」村正「ふっ。無様ね、御堂！」景明「どう見てもお前の方が余りにも必死だ」村正「そんなこと言っていられるのも今の間よ！
　お……男の人の体はこういうのに耐えられ
ないようにできてるんでしょっ」村正「こうすれば、すぐ――」

en:
With the expression of a diver running out of air, Muramasa returned to the game.

Finesse, there was none. But by accident or instinct she had found precisely the sort of opening that demanded an answer.

I began studying the board.
ja:
素潜りの最中、酸素不足に陥った時のような顔で、
村正が息遣いを乱しながら行為を再開する。
　俺の男性器を掌握する指が、拙くも動いた。

　手管とはまるで無縁。
　しかし偶然か本能的なものか、力加減は絶妙だった。

　粘膜に程良い加減の刺激を受け、結果、血がそこへ
流れ込む。

en: Muramasa"ARRE, BHOSDIKE! You moved ONE piece! Why is the whole bloody board threatening me?!"Kageaki"That is a remarkably irresponsible question."Muramasa"I-is this how it works?!"Kageaki"Generally... What did you think would happen?"Muramasa"..."Muramasa"..."Muramasa"ACCORDING TO PLAN! I have merely not reached the part where the plan makes SENSE!"Kageaki(She is trying much too hard...)Muramasa"Wait... that one too... there also..."Kageaki"..."Muramasa"H-hah! See? Plenty of energy you have!"Kageaki"Whatever you are trying to prove, I am certainly healthier than you look on the verge of suffocation."Muramasa"Th-this is the point! However much you deny it, question it, look down on it—"Muramasa"A living thing is ALIVE! I will not let you call that meaningless!"Kageaki"..."Muramasa"If you think you are base, then live as a base person!"Kageaki"...Muramasa."Muramasa"Consider yourself dust. Admit you don't have the strength to carry every crime, every responsibility."Muramasa"I will bring you down from that height."
ja:
村正「きゃー!?
　なんで大きくなるのっ！」景明「そんな無責任な事を言われても困る」村正「こっ、こういうものなの!?」景明「まぁ……こういうものだが。
　どうなると思っていたんだ」村正「……」村正「…………」村正「予定通りよ！」景明（必死過ぎる……）村正「わ……まだ、むくむくって」景明「……」村正「ふっ、ふふふ！
　ほ、ほーら、元気なものじゃないっ」景明「何がほらなのかはともかく、酸欠一歩手前
のお前より健康そうなのは確かだ」村正「こ……こういうことよ。
　貴方がどんなに否定したって、疑問をぶつ
けたって、卑しんだって――」村正「生きてるものは生きてるんだから！
　それに意味が無いなんて言わせない！」景明「…………」村正「卑しいと思うなら、卑しいなりに生きれば
いいでしょ！」景明「……村正」村正「塵芥だと思えばいい。
　罪も責任も、自分には背負う力なんて無い
んだって認めればいい」村正「私が――貴方を貶おとしめてあげるから」

en: The grand strategy was now in serious difficulty. Muramasa's expression darkened with concentration, and she shifted for a better view of the board.
ja:
村正の衣服が解ほどけた。
　射干玉ぬばたまを溶いたような肌が露わになる。

　そんな無防備な姿になって、村正は俺の上に跨またがろう
とした。

en: Kageaki"Enough now..."Muramasa"..."

My automatic objection received no answer.

She considered a move. Reconsidered it. Considered it some more.

The pieces were enjoying a very restful game.
ja:
反射的に制止するも、返答はない。
　肉と肉が、わずかに触れ合う。

　そこで――そのまま。
　接触の密度を微妙に変化させるのみで、それ以上の
進展はしなかった。

en: Muramasa"...Tch..."

No, this was not some cunning technique. She was simply afraid of committing herself to unfamiliar ground.

The board waited. So did I. Most of the battle was taking place between Muramasa and Muramasa.
ja:
微妙な交渉が性感を煽る。
　俺のその部分は反応を示し――村正もそうだった。

　どちらの発とも知れない粘液が、間隙に糸を引く。

　しかしそれは、性の技巧としてされている行為では
なかった。
　単に村正は――おそらく未知への恐れから――躊躇
して、こうしているに過ぎない。

en: Kageaki"That is enough, no...? Leave it there."Muramasa"W-what? You don't like it?"Kageaki"Not that, but this—"Muramasa"You made me take over your work the other night."Kageaki"Ugh..."Muramasa"Demanding all that help—and then you left the whole business halfway!"Muramasa"Aaah, now I remember it and I'm angry all over again!"Kageaki"At that time..."Muramasa"CHUP! This is what you wanted, isn't it? Somebody to stay and help..."
ja:
景明「もういいだろう……止めておけ」村正「な、なによっ。
　嫌なの？」景明「嫌ではないが、これは――」村正「一度、私のこと押し倒したくせに」景明「う……」村正「あ、あんなことして――
　途中で放り出して！」村正「あーもう、思い出したらまた腹立ってきた
じゃないの！」景明「あの時は……」村正「うるさいだまれ！
　こっ――こうしたかったんでしょ……」

en:
At last she committed herself.

One decisive move, and an opening in her position lay exposed.
ja:
思い切ったのか。
　村正の体から力が抜け、体重が落ちてきた。

　肉の尖塔が秘洞にめり込み、引っ掛かり――
　突き破る。

en: Muramasa"Tch..."Muramasa"...Oh..."Kageaki"Fool..."
ja: 村正「くっ……」村正「……うぅー……」景明「馬鹿……」

en:
I muttered it. The mistake in her position was plain to see.

She had told me that her transformed body reproduced her former self. It had not, apparently, come with a certificate in board-game mastery.
ja:
呟く。
　結合部から滴したたる、朱色の液体が見えた。

　村正の肉体変成は、劒冑になる以前の姿を再現する
ものだと云っていた。
　往時の村正に性交渉の経験が無かったなら――当然、
こういう事になるだろう。

en: Muramasa"I'm not the fool! YOU are!"Kageaki"What are you gaining by forcing yourself like this?"Muramasa"I'm not forcing anything...!"Muramasa"You enjoy winning, no? Fine! Play your ferocious game however you like!"Kageaki"Even if you say that..."
ja:
村正「馬鹿じゃないっ。
　馬鹿は、貴方っ」景明「そんな無理をしてどうする」村正「無理なんかしてない……っ」村正「こ――こういう事が気持ちいいんでしょう。
　構わないから、その凶暴なので好きなよう
にしたらいいのよっ」景明「そう言われてもだな」

en:
Muramasa knew far too little about the game. Blunder after blunder, and still she tried to continue. This was nowhere near the confident demonstration she had intended.

At this rate, the game would eventually collapse by itself. Whatever determination she applied, she would have no way to keep playing.

That would be fine...◆ of course it would. But...
ja:
村正は余りに無知だ。
　痛みを堪こらえて動こうとしているが……それは性的な
快感をもたらすものには程遠い。

　元々、湿りの少ないところへ無理矢理挿入したのだ。
　過剰な摩擦による痛みは、俺も共有するものだった。

　このままでいれば、いずれ俺の男性部分は力を失い、
村正がどう頑張って行為を続けようとしても続けられ
なくなるだろう。
　無論、それでいい……◆のだ、が…………

en: Muramasa"Tch... oh..."Kageaki"..."Muramasa"Ah..."Kageaki"..."Kageaki"Muramasa."Muramasa"Eh...?"Kageaki"There is no need to rush at it so violently. Slow down."Kageaki"Gently. Consider what each move leaves behind."Muramasa"L-like this...?"
ja:
村正「つっ……くぅ……」景明「…………」村正「あぅ……」景明「…………」景明「村正」村正「え……？」景明「そう乱暴に動かなくていい。
　力を抜いて、速度を緩めろ」景明「軽く柔らかく、擦るように」村正「こ……こう……？」

en:
She changed her play as instructed. Still inexperienced, yes, but the disasters were considerably reduced.

When one player lacked experience, both needed to show some restraint. Otherwise, where was the game?
ja:
言われるまま、村正が動きを変える。
　拙い事に変わりはなかったが、それで苦痛はかなり
和らいだ。

　女性の側に経験が少ない時は、とにかく双方が力を
抑えないと、快楽を得るどころではなくなる。

en: Kageaki"And don't hold your breath. Keep breathing normally."Muramasa"Y-yes..."
ja:
景明「それと、息は止めない方がいい。
　軽く浅く、呼吸を続けておけ」村正「う、うん……」

en: She would stop breathing from concentration, which only made her more tense. Seeing that she had a little room to think now, I reached toward the board and pointed out a possibility she had missed.
ja:
苦痛に耐えようとすると自然、息は止まるが、息が
止まると体の力も抜けなくなる。
　だからこのような場合は余計に痛みが増す。

　多少の余裕が出てきたのを見て、俺は繋がる部分に
片手を伸ばした。
　淫核を探り当て、触れる。

en: Muramasa"Ah!"
ja: 村正「あ――っ」

en:
She started. Had that move never occurred to her?

An unfamiliar idea might give her a fright, but at least it would take her attention off the previous disaster. I carefully showed her the simplest continuation.

Her pieces came together in a defence.
ja:
村正の体が跳ねた。
　自分で触れた事もなかったのか。

　未知の刺激は苦痛に近いかもしれないが、それでも
破瓜の痛みを散らす役には立つだろう。
　俺は爪を引っ掛けないように注意しつつ、ごく軽く
愛撫した。

　きゅい、と村正の膣が締まる。

en: Muramasa"Oh...!"Kageaki"You don't like this...?"Muramasa"No! That isn't it...!"Muramasa"Never mind me. You should—"Kageaki"...I see."
ja:
村正「うっ、ん……！」景明「嫌か……？」村正「嫌じゃないっ……
　嫌じゃない、けど……！」村正「っ……私のことは、いいから。
　貴方が――っ」景明「……そうか」

en:
Then I remembered why she had started all this.

This was not the answer she was asking for.

I stopped arranging her defence for her. Instead, I played my own game. By now, the bottle had ceased to matter.

Small, incisive moves. For my own satisfaction only.
ja:
思い出す。
　村正が、こんな事をした理由。

　応える方法は、こうあるべきではなかった。

　両腕で、村正の腰の動きを止めさせる。
　入れ替わりに、俺自身を動かす。

　鋼糸は既に拘束力の殆どを失っていた。
　妨げにはならない。

　小刻みに、抉るように突き込む。
　自分の享楽だけを求めて。

en: Muramasa"Ah— Oh...!"
ja: 村正「はッ――んっ、くぅ」

en:
At the state of the board, she looked close to tears. Even that I accepted as a small victory.

Excitement. The petty pleasure of getting the better of someone.

No restraining myself so that she could enjoy herself more. Winning was what I wanted, and winning was what I pursued.

Fully absorbed in this undignified occupation.
Right to the limit.
ja:
身を裂かれる苦しさに村正が涙する。
　瞳が潤んで、雫がこぼれた。

　俺の口元へ落ちる、それすら甘露と受け取る。

　昂ぶる。
　凌辱の高揚。

　己の欲を抑えて、相手の快楽を引き上げてやりなど
しない。
　ただただ、突き上げる欲望のみを追う。

　その卑しい行為に没頭し切る。

　限界へ。
　極限まで。

en: Muramasa"Ah... oh..."
ja: 村正「あ……あぅ」

en:
Something dark filled my chest. Something unworthy.

The joy of being unbearably pleased with myself.
ja:
黒いもの。
　汚穢きたないもので、胸を満たす。

　嗜虐の喜び。

en:
Yes.
That was it.

What had I been hesitating over? What was all that anguish for?

I was a man who could enjoy this. A human being who knew these petty pleasures perfectly well.

Another move. Her dismay. My mouth smiling.

Fun. Happiness. Satisfaction.

Ah.
One more move.
ja:
――そう。
　そうだった。

　何を迷っていたのか。
　何を悩んでいたのか。

　俺はこういうモノを味わえる男だった。

　下卑た悦楽を知る人間だった。

　突き上げる。
　健気な女が泣く。

　俺の唇が笑う。

　楽しい。
　嬉しい。
　心地良い。

　ああ。
　貫く。

en: Muramasa"Mido!"
ja: 村正「御堂――――っ」

en:
The game ended. That ridiculous little contest had exhausted body and mind alike.

Perfect satisfaction.

For that instant, I had certainly found a reason to be alive.
ja:
絶頂に達する。
　肉体と精神のそれを同時に極めて。

　完璧な喜悦。
　俺はその瞬間、確かに、生きる意味を得ていた。

en:
Afterward, we lay exhausted beside the table.

And I despaired properly.

No value to my life, no right to it—such grand judgments I could deliver about myself. Then turn around and gorge on pleasure without shame. This was the person making those judgments.

Despair.

...What a low fellow. Really.

And yet—◆
once I accepted it, that was all there was to it.

Nothing felt out of place.

Apparently this was who I had been all along.
ja:
……そうして。
　村正と共に虚脱の中で横たわり。
　
　俺は正しく絶望した。

　生きる価値無し、資格無しと思いながら、恥知らず
に快楽を貪り耽溺できる――
　この、自分自身というもの。

　絶望する。
　
　……何とも。これは何とも卑しい。

　そして。◆
　受け入れてしまえば、それはそれだけの事に過ぎな
かった。

　違和感は何も無い。

　この己とは、そういうものだったのだと思う。

en: Kageaki"Muramasa."Muramasa"...Hm..."Kageaki"You are completely absurd."
ja: 景明「村正」村正「……ん……」景明「お前は、滅茶苦茶だ」

en:
I tugged her ear. Still distracted, she grumbled in protest.

Honestly... I had never heard of encouragement being delivered in this fashion. Even clumsiness should have some limit.

But—
For the first time—

I found it dear.
That clumsiness. That single-minded devotion from my companion who was not human.
ja:
耳を引っ張る。
　上の空ながらも不満げに、村正が喉で唸った。

　全く……こんな励まし方は聞いた事もない。
　不器用にも程がある。

　だが。
　
　
　――――初めて。

　愛しいと、そう思った。
　この不器用さが。

　人ならぬ伴侶の一途さが。

en: Kageaki"Muramasa..."Muramasa"..."Kageaki"Will you stay with me?"Muramasa"..."Muramasa"...Yes..."
ja: 景明「村正……」村正「…………」景明「一緒にいてくれるか」村正「……………………」村正「…………うん…………」

en:
I had found some peace. Something I had not known since killing Hikaru—no, since killing my foster mother. It had been absent for so long.

The warmth beside me felt precious.

Once, I had wanted the coldness of iron from Muramasa. Now, from the very same person, I wanted the warmth of a living companion.

...Truly, there was no saving me from myself.

I laughed at that.

Sleepiness came. I sank into gentle mud.

For the first time in two years, I slept deeply.
ja:
安らぎを得ていた。
　光を殺して以来――いや養母を殺して以来、絶えて
久しかったそれ。

　腕の中の体温を貴重に思う。

　嘗て己は、村正に、鉄の冷たさを求めた筈だった。
　翻って今は、同じ相手に、肉の温もりを求めようと
している。

　……つくづく、駄目だな。
　
　そう嗤う。

　眠気が訪れた。

　優しい泥濘の中へ沈む。
　二年ぶりに、俺は熟睡した。

en:
I woke in the morning sunlight. Muramasa was no longer beside me.

Instead, I heard the brisk, pleasant tapping of a knife on a chopping board.
ja:
朝の日差しを浴びて目覚めると、既に村正は傍らに
いなかった。
　代わりに、俎板まないたを打つ小気味良い音が聴こえていた。

en: Kageaki"...Are you making breakfast?"Muramasa"Yes. Wait a little, na."
ja:
景明「……朝食を作っているのか？」村正「ええ。
　少し待っていて」

en:
Was this what they called a possessing spirit leaving the body? My own body, my own mind, and both had become so light that I was finding them unfamiliar.

Alive. Bas, that was the feeling.

No additional importance was coming attached to it.

Small.
Not heavy.
Someone, and no one in particular.

Just living.

...So in the end, had I been arrogant? Had I only now agreed to recognise myself at my actual size?

It seemed that way.

The way of heaven.
That phrase from last night came back to me.
ja:
憑物つきものが落ちた心地、と云うのだろうか。
　心身の軽さは、我が事ながら戸惑う程だった。

　生きている。
　ただ、そう感じる。

　そこに付加価値は何も無い。

　小さく。
　重からず。
　何者でもあり、何者でもなく。

　ただ生きている。

　……とどのつまり。
　自分は傲慢だったのかと、思う。

　等身大の自分自身を、今ようやく認めているのか。
　そう思う。

　――天道。
　昨夜聞いた一語を思い出す。

en: Kageaki"..."

If a person's sins were for heaven to judge—and for the collective judgment of the world below, which reflected heaven—then what was I doing, taking the whole judgment into my own personal hands? That itself was arrogance.◆

...Was that the matter?

Probably... yes.

One day I would be judged. The day of reckoning would come; I believed that.

With that belief—

I would live.
ja:
人の罪業が、天、そして天を映す俗世ちじょうの衆知の裁量
するところであるなら、俺自身、俺個人でそれを云々
する事こそ不遜。◆
　――――か。

　おそらく……そうなのであろう。

　いずれこの身は裁かれる。
　報いの日は来ると信じる。
　
　――信じて、

　生きる。

en: Kageaki(Achha. So that is how it is.)
ja: 景明（そういう事か）

en:
Probably that was how it was.

The kitchen's cheerful rhythm came to my ears, and something filled me. Happiness—◆no. That was not quite the thing. But peace was there. A quietness inside.

Like soaking in a lake in summer. Time could pass at its own speed; I was in no hurry to assist it...
ja:
そういう事なのであろう。

　台所からの軽快な調べに耳を委ねながら。
　俺は幸福――◆とは、異なる。しかし平穏な、静謐な
もので内面が満たされているのを感じた。

　夏の湖水に浸かる心地で、緩やかな時を過ごす……。

en:
And in this manner—

One hour passed.
ja:
そうして。
　一時間が経過した。

en: Kageaki"..."Kageaki"Still... not ready?"
Muramasa"J-just a little more."Kageaki"Achha. No, please don't take it as hurrying from my side."
ja:
村正「も、もうちょっと」景明「そうか。
　いや、別に急かしたのではないから」

en:
...

Somewhere, on some occasion, I had heard a thing.

In a tsurugi-smithing family, whoever was chosen to inherit the name spent almost their whole life learning the craft, from very early childhood onward. For learning anything else, time was practically not available.

Ordinary household work went entirely to the apprentices and servants.

...This was what I had heard.
ja:
…………。
　そう言えば、何処かで何かの折に聞いた事がある。

　劒冑鍛冶の家門に生まれ、銘なの継承者と見做された
者は、ごく幼少の頃からその後の生涯ほぼ全てを鍛冶
技術の修行に費やすため――
　他の諸事を学ぶゆとりは皆無に等しく。

　日常生活の雑事は門弟、下人らに任せ切りになる。
　
　…………と。

en: Kageaki"..."

Now put this information beside the present situation.

Muramasa had cooked before, hadn't she?

Even once?
ja:
以上を踏まえて考えてみる。

　村正は果たして、料理をした事があるのだろうか・・・・・・・・・・・・・・？

en: Kageaki"...That sound..."
ja: 景明「……音が……」

en: Muramasa"Little more. Bas, little more, na."Kageaki"Y-yes."
ja: 村正「もう少し。もう少しね」景明「あ、ああ」

en: Kageaki"..."
An axe and a hammer were not, to my knowledge, included in this kitchen's equipment...
ja:
この家の台所に斧やハンマーの用意は無かった筈だ
が……。

en: Muramasa"THODA SA AUR! LITTLE MORE!"
ja: 村正「もう少し！」

en: Kageaki"...A Gatling gun...?"
ja: 景明「……ガトリングガン……？」

en: Or was the equipment actually a rock drill...?
ja: いや削岩機か……？

en: Muramasa《ABHI! It is coming now only!》Kageaki"Yes..."
ja: 村正《すぐ！　すぐだから！》景明「ああ……」

en: Kageaki"..."

A very familiar giant spider seemed to pass across my vision just now, a pot, a knife, a ladle and various other things distributed among all eight legs...

An illusion, obviously. As far as I knew, two arms were supposed to cover the whole cooking requirement.
ja:
今、八本の節足あしに鍋と包丁とおたまとその他諸々を
持った馴染み深いでっかい蜘蛛が視界を過よぎったよう
に思えたが……無論、錯覚であろう。
　俺の知る限り、料理には二本の腕で足りる筈である。

en:
...

Finished, at last...?
ja:
……………………。

　ようやく終わったか……。

en: Muramasa《...Begin the end. Enact death. Reveal the void...》Kageaki"ARRE KYUN?! BREAKFAST HAI, WHY ARE WE ENDING EXISTENCE?!"
ja: 村正《……蒐窮開闢おわりをはじめる。終焉執行しをおこなう。虚無発現そらをあらわす……》景明「何故だァァァ!?」

en:
...Finally I also put my hands to the work.

The meal arrived as something less like breakfast and more like a slightly early lunch.
ja:
……結局俺が手伝い、朝食というより少し早い昼食
になった。

en: Muramasa"N-no, aisa nahi hai. Cooking I can do, okay!"Muramasa"Only... dekho, these tools are different from before. Ingredients also. That is why! A little confusion happened because of that, bas!"Kageaki"...I see."
ja:
村正「ち、違うのよ。
　これでも料理くらいできるんだから！」村正「ただ……ほら、道具や食材が昔と違うし。
　それでよ！　それでちょっと戸惑っただけ
なの！」景明「……そうか」

en:
Knives, chopping boards, pots. Rice, miso, dried horse mackerel. I was fairly sure these had been available five hundred years ago also.

I did not contribute this information. I nodded.

Indeed, without some explanation of that sort, it was difficult to understand how breakfast had resulted in half a kitchen.
ja:
包丁も俎板も鍋も、米も味噌も鯵あじの干物も、五百年
前から存在していると思うのだが。
　言わずにおき、俺は頷いた。

　実際そんな理由でも無ければ、厨房半壊という結末
は納得が難しい。

en: Muramasa"Tomorrow I'll do it properly!"Kageaki"No. Kindly contain this ambition."
ja: 村正「明日はちゃんとやるからっ」景明「いや自重してくれ」

en: Any further improvement of this kind, and Makimura might return home directly into cardiac arrest.
ja:
あれ以上の惨状にしては、牧村さんが戻られたとき
心停止を起こしかねない。

en: Muramasa"But—"Kageaki"Breakfast I can do without."Muramasa"That is not good for your health, you know."Kageaki"...And stopping a tsurugi doing an electromagnetic draw with a kitchen cleaver was some health treatment for me?"Muramasa"Hmph..."
ja:
村正「でも」景明「俺は朝飯を抜いても平気な方だ」村正「それ、健康に良くないのよ」景明「……出刃包丁で電磁抜刀しようとする劒冑
を止めるのも余り健康的な体験ではなかった
んだが」村正「むぅ……」

en:
Muramasa put out her lower lip in protest. Several children ran past her.

Sunday, before noon. The sky completely clear. For a walk, the weather could hardly improve upon this.

I had called Muramasa outside with no particular destination. Walking itself seemed sufficient. We were not required to achieve some great thing on the way.
ja:
不平そうに口を尖らせる村正。
　その脇を、数人の子供達が駆けていった。

　日曜の昼前。空は抜けるような晴天。
　散歩には絶好の日和といえる。

　特に目的もなく村正を誘って外へ出たが、ただ歩く
だけでも充分に心地良さを楽しめそうだ。

en: Muramasa"...Such nice weather, na."Kageaki"If winter maintained this standard, I would have no serious objection to it."Muramasa"You don't like the cold?"Kageaki"I have the normal human objection, yes."Kageaki"Heat troubles me more, though..."Muramasa"For me it was cold, I think. Now I am a tsurugi, so neither is a problem."Kageaki"As the saying goes, in winter you can put on more clothes and heat the room. Summer does not become bearable even after you have removed everything. In your time, did nobody make this observation?"Muramasa"No... but I understand the point."Muramasa"Only, listen..."Kageaki"Hm?"Muramasa"Every time you feel cold, you keep burning fuel, and the expense, uff. It really adds up. In winter you had to decide: warm yourself and accept less food, or eat and stay cold."Muramasa"So winter has not left me such happy memories."Kageaki"Ah... I see."
ja:
村正「……いい陽気ね」景明「いつもこうなら、冬も悪くない」村正「寒いのは嫌いなの？」景明「まあそうだな。人並みに」景明「寒さよりは、暑さの方が苦手だが……」村正「私は寒い方が嫌いだったかしら。
　今は劒冑こんなだから、どちらも平気だけど」景明「冬の寒さは着込んで暖房を利かせれば耐え
られるが、夏の暑さは裸になっても耐え難い
……などと云うがな。
　お前の時代には、そんな言葉は無かったか」村正「無いけど……
　わかる気はする」村正「でもねぇ」景明「ん？」村正「寒いからって火を使ってばかりいると……
費えが嵩むのよ。もう本当に。
　だから冬は、食い扶持が減るのを覚悟して
温もるか、その逆かになるわけ」村正「お陰で冬にはいい思い出が無いのよね」景明「あぁ……成程」

en:
Even a conversation about feeling cold had found the five-hundred-year gap. I had offered one very wise solution: heat the room. Haan. Magnificent. Had I considered that fuel had a price, or was my wisdom supposed to burn by itself?

Winter fuel bills troubled housewives now also. In her time, the fuel was less developed and more expensive; naturally the trouble would have been greater.

Five hundred years of progress, and still the householder's choice: warm stomach, cold hands, or warm hands, empty stomach. The seasons had changed repeatedly. This particular joke had not.
ja:
時代背景の違いがこんなところでも。
　現代も冬場の光熱費は主婦の悩みの種だが、燃料が
未発達かつ高価だった昔は尚一層難儀な問題であって
当然である。

en: Muramasa"Summer heat, at least, you cannot do anything about. From the beginning itself you can say chhodo and give up."Kageaki"You have arrived at the argument from the opposite direction."Muramasa"Well... still..."Kageaki"Yes."Muramasa"Spring and autumn are better than both, obviously."Kageaki"On that point, complete agreement."Muramasa"Somewhere across the sea there are countries where spring goes on all year, no?"Kageaki"Yes."Muramasa"If we could live there... how nice that would be."Kageaki"Yes. Though a little... lonely also, perhaps."Muramasa"...Achha. No watching the four seasons change. That pleasure would go."Kageaki"Summer nights, winter scenery. Complain as I may, I would be sorry to lose them."Muramasa"Then learning to accept things is the main matter? Otherwise we start asking for luxury and the demands will never finish."Kageaki"Who can say? Perhaps science will advance until we can choose whichever season we like."Kageaki"Then make any demand. All shall be satisfied. Human wisdom will have achieved victory."Muramasa"Yes."Kageaki"Indeed."Muramasa"..."Kageaki"..."Muramasa"One minute. Are we actually losing and calling it our victory?"
ja:
村正「その点、夏の暑さはどうにもならないぶん
最初から諦めがつくし」景明「逆の発想だな」村正「まぁ……でも」景明「うむ」村正「春と秋の方がいいに決まってるけど」景明「全くだ」村正「海の向こうのどこかには、常春の国もある
んでしょう？」景明「ああ」村正「そんな所に住めたら幸せね」景明「そうだな。
　少し……寂しい気もするが」村正「……そっか。
　四季の風情の移り変わりも楽しめないって
ことだものね」景明「夏の夜も冬景色も、失うとなれば惜しい」村正「つまり諦めが肝心で、贅沢を言い始めると
切りがないってことかしら」景明「さて？
　いずれ科学の進歩で、好みの季節を自由に
選べるようになるかもしれん」景明「そうなればどんな要求でも叶う。
　人類の叡智の勝利だ」村正「そうね」景明「うむ」村正「…………」景明「…………」村正「それ……実は勝ったつもりで負けてない？」

en: Kageaki"You are also getting that impression."Muramasa"The charm seems to have gone somewhere..."Kageaki"Yes. On charm, we have suffered a total loss..."
ja: 景明「やはりそう思うか」村正「風情が無いような……」景明「風情は無いな……」

en:
What were we talking about? Nothing of importance.

Not moving our mouths because there was something to say. Finding something to say because the mouths wanted to keep moving.

And walking like that.

Going nowhere in particular.

No purpose was being served by this time. Worthless, though, I did not consider it.

Let it continue like this. That was what I wanted.
ja:
他愛もない会話。

　話すために口を動かすというより、口を動かすため
に話すかのような。
　
　そうして、歩く。

　あても無く。

　意義を持たない時間。
　しかし、無価値とは思わなかった。

　こうしていたいと思った。

en: Muramasa"Mido, look."Kageaki"Hm...?"Muramasa"What is that?"Kageaki"The park? ...There's a crowd gathering."Kageaki"Shall we go and see?"Muramasa"Yes."
ja:
村正「ね、御堂」景明「ん……？」村正「あれ、何かしら」景明「公園か？
　……人が集まっているな」景明「行ってみるか」村正「うん」

en:
